author: loci-dev
body:
Mirrored from ggml-org/llama.cpp#17875

Follow-up to https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/17558 .

I forgot that the tile kernel would also be suffering the same problem with overflows. Unfortunately unlike the vector kernel the tile kernel is compute bound rather than I/O bound so simply switching the arithmetic to FP32 is not a good option. I think the least bad option is to scale down Q and to then scale up KQ afterwards again. The tradeoff is potentially flushing some small values < $2^{-12}$ to zero. Affected GPUs are P100s, V100s, and RDNA1 or older AMD GPUs.

body:
This pull request refactors the sound and high score logic in the Cannon Game app, focusing on improving code clarity and enhancing the way high scores are handled. The most notable changes are the refactoring of the high score method to return more detailed information, adjustments to sound triggers based on score type, and cleanup of comments and code structure related to sound management.

**High Score Logic Improvements:**

* The `HighScoreManager.addScore` method now returns an integer indicating the type of score achieved (0 = not added, 1 = added but not first place, 2 = new first place), instead of a boolean. This allows for more nuanced handling of score events.
* The game now checks the returned score type from `addScore` to determine which sound to play: a special sound for a new first place score and a regular game over sound otherwise.

**Sound Management and Code Cleanup:**

* Removed unnecessary comments and clarified code related to `MediaPlayer` and `SoundPool` initialization, improving readability. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-b124ff034f4b48658baeb1760340aec6c0ac7f1328bbfc7b78a044654d8a3a1fL92-R92) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-b124ff034f4b48658baeb1760340aec6c0ac7f1328bbfc7b78a044654d8a3a1fL112) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-b124ff034f4b48658baeb1760340aec6c0ac7f1328bbfc7b78a044654d8a3a1fL128) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-b124ff034f4b48658baeb1760340aec6c0ac7f1328bbfc7b78a044654d8a3a1fL446)

**Game Initialization Logic:**

* Updated the `newGame` method to reset game state variables only when starting at level 1, ensuring proper score and shot tracking across levels.

author: chrislusf
body:
## Summary

This PR addresses the issue raised in https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/discussions/7653

When using `AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity` with tokens from identity providers like GitLab CI, the ID Token has an `exp` claim limited to the CI job's timeout. Previously, SeaweedFS would issue STS sessions that could outlive the source token's expiration.

## Changes

This PR implements the principle: **"if calculated exp > incoming exp claim, then limit outgoing exp to incoming exp"**

### Files Changed

1. **`weed/iam/providers/provider.go`**
   - Added `TokenExpiration *time.Time` field to `ExternalIdentity` struct

2. **`weed/iam/oidc/oidc_provider.go`**
   - Extract `exp`, `iat`, and `nbf` claims in `ValidateToken` and populate `TokenClaims`
   - Pass token expiration from `Authenticate` to `ExternalIdentity.TokenExpiration`

3. **`weed/iam/sts/sts_service.go`**
   - Modified `calculateSessionDuration` to accept an optional `tokenExpiration` parameter
   - Cap the session duration to not exceed the source token's expiration
   - Added logging when session duration is limited

4. **`weed/iam/sts/sts_service_test.go`**
   - Added `TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration` with various scenarios
   - Added `TestAssumeRoleWithWebIdentityRespectsTokenExpiration` for end-to-end testing

## Behavior

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| No token expiration | Use configured default duration |
| Token expires before default duration | Cap at token expiration |
| Token expires after default duration | Use default duration |
| Requested duration shorter than token expiry | Use requested duration |
| Requested duration longer than token expiry | Cap at token expiration |
| GitLab CI 5-minute token | Session capped at 5 minutes |

## Testing

All existing tests pass, plus new tests specifically for this behavior:

```
=== RUN   TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration
=== RUN   TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration/no_token_expiration_-_use_default_duration
=== RUN   TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration/token_expires_before_default_duration
=== RUN   TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration/token_expires_after_default_duration_-_use_default
=== RUN   TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration/requested_duration_shorter_than_token_expiry
=== RUN   TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration/requested_duration_longer_than_token_expiry_-_cap_at_token_expiry
=== RUN   TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration/GitLab_CI_short-lived_token_scenario
--- PASS: TestSessionDurationCappedByTokenExpiration (0.00s)
=== RUN   TestAssumeRoleWithWebIdentityRespectsTokenExpiration
--- PASS: TestAssumeRoleWithWebIdentityRespectsTokenExpiration (0.00s)
```

Fixes: https://github.com/seaweedfs/seaweedfs/discussions/7653

author: samjdurante
body:
### Summary
We noticed that after migrating to Apollo V2, graphQL requests using the .NetworkOnly fetchBehavior seemed to still be returning a cached version. 

Turns out that Apollo was not adding the cachePolicy to the URLRequest, so the URLRequests were going out with the default .useProtocolCachePolicy set as the cache policy.

### Steps to reproduce
- Make a graphQL request using the .networkOnly fetchBehavior
- Check the URLRequest's cachePolicy
```request.cachePolicy.rawValue``` logged as 0 (.useProtocolCachePolicy) when it should be 1 (.reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData)

### Previous Fix
We encountered this a while ago in Apollo V1, which ended up getting fixed, but the bug seems to have been reintroduced when Apollo switched to fetchBehavior in V2
- Issue: https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-ios/issues/3432
- Commit: https://github.com/apollographql/apollo-ios-dev/pull/476/commits/511b76aa4bd7ee85917fd5913214c81286088927

author: faithmry
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes 11 bugs across multiple artifacts that were causing runtime errors during iOS forensic data extraction. The fixes address datetime parsing issues, missing table/column handling, and type validation problems.

## Bugs Fixed

### Datetime/ISO Format Issues (6 bugs)
1. **bluetoothPairedReg** - Fixed `NameError: name 'UTC' is not defined`
   - Changed import and function call from `convert_unix_ts_to_str` to `convert_unix_ts_to_utc`

2. **alarms** - Fixed `ValueError: Invalid isoformat string` with 'Z' suffix
   - Modified `convert_plist_date_to_utc()` in ilapfuncs.py (line 1160)
   - Removed 'Z' suffix from datetime format string

3. **dhcpLeases** - Fixed `ValueError: Invalid isoformat string` with 'Z' suffix
   - Modified `convert_plist_date_to_timezone_offset()` in ilapfuncs.py (line 1149)
   - Removed 'Z' suffix from datetime format string

4-5. **keyboardAppUsage & appleWifiKnownNetworksTimes** - Fixed by change in ilapfuncs.py.

### Type Validation Issues (2 bugs)
6. **user_defaults** - Fixed `AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'items'`
   - Added `isinstance(plist, dict)` check before calling `.items()`
   - Prevents error when plist is 'INVALID FILE' string

7. **system_version_plist** - Fixed `TypeError: expected str, bytes or os.PathLike object, not function`
   - Changed variable assignment from function name to actual file path
   - `data_source = system_version_plist` → `data_source = plist_file`

### Database Schema Issues (4 bugs)
8. **photosDbexif** - Fixed `OperationalError: no such table: ZASSET`
   - Added table existence check before querying
   - Gracefully skips databases without ZASSET table

9. **parseCDCache** - Fixed `OperationalError: no such column: score`
   - Added column existence check using PRAGMA
   - Handles both iOS 13.4.1 and newer schema versions

10. **trustedPeers** - Fixed `OperationalError: no such table: ZESCROWCLIENTMETADATA`
    - Added table existence check before querying
    - Returns early if table doesn't exist

11. **sysdiagnose** - Fixed `AttributeError: 'Context' has no attribute 'get_model_name'`
    - Changed to correct method name: `get_device_model()`

body:
## References
* Fixes #11634 

## Description
This pull request handles the deprecation of `AntPathRequestMatcher` by replacing all its usages with the recommended [`PathPatternRequestMatcher`](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/site/docs/current/api/org/springframework/security/web/servlet/util/matcher/PathPatternRequestMatcher.html). This migration in the Spring Security configuration ensures future compatibility without altering existing behavior.

## Instructions for Reviewers

List of changes in this PR:
* **Replaced Deprecated Class:** All usages of `AntPathRequestMatcher` have been replaced with the recommended `PathPatternRequestMatcher`.
* **Updated [`StatelessLoginFilter.java`](https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/main/dspace-server-webapp/src/main/java/org/dspace/app/rest/security/StatelessLoginFilter.java):**
  * The filter's constructor now uses `PathPatternRequestMatcher` to define the URL and HTTP method it responds to.
* **Updated [WebSecurityConfiguration.java](https://github.com/DSpace/DSpace/blob/main/dspace-server-webapp/src/main/java/org/dspace/app/rest/security/WebSecurityConfiguration.java):**
  * Modified the `requestMatchers()` call for the `/actuator/info` endpoint to use `PathPatternRequestMatcher`.
  * Updated the logout configuration such that `logoutRequestMatcher()` uses `PathPatternRequestMatcher` for the `/api/authn/logout` endpoint.

**No Functional Changes**: This is a pure migration. All existing automated tests pass; manual testing needed to confirm that the behavior (e.g. logout, etc) remains unchanged.

author: mkeesey
body:
Fix databaseExists call and speed up kustainer creates and tear downs

Kustainer spawns Kusto through bash, so the normal shutdown signals do
not get passed through. This means that the processes take 10s to
shutdown after timeouts. Instead, create the container with an init
process that can adopt the Kusto process with bash exits and can reap
the process.

Potential fix for [https://github.com/novaferrydianto/vuln-bank/security/code-scanning/17](https://github.com/novaferrydianto/vuln-bank/security/code-scanning/17)

The best way to fix the problem is to enforce proper parameterization on *every* query submitted to `execute_query`. This means:
- Disallow any query strings that show signs of having been built via string formatting or f-strings or `.format()`.
- Require that every query string uses `%s` placeholders only and that parameters are supplied via the second argument.
- In `execute_query`, add checks similar to those in `execute_transaction` that scan for unsafe construction patterns, such as `{}`, `%` not followed by `s` or `%`, or concatenation.
- If unsafe patterns are detected, raise an exception, preventing unsafe SQL construction from ever reaching the database.
- Edit the `execute_query` function in `database.py` to add these checks, immediately before `cursor.execute`. Do not alter the rest of the function or the way `params` and `fetch` are handled.

  - Cambiar estado de usuario
  - Obtener servicio por codigo
  - Actualizar servicio por ID
  - Listar estados de solicitudes
- **Correcciones SQL**:
  - Se cambio INNER JOIN a LEFT JOIN en getServices para mostrar servicios sin formularios asignados
  - Se optimizo el conteo total de solicitudes usando COUNT(*) directo para mayor precision
  - Se elimino el retorno de la columna id (inexistente) tras la actualizacion
### Frontend
- **Gestion de Empleados**:
  - Conexion a API para crear usuarios y correccion de envio de datos
  - Edicion de Rol y Estado funcional con datos reales
- **Gestion de Servicios**:
  - Catalogo conectado a backend
  - Correccion de ID en actualizaciones y visualizacion documentos
- **Dashboard**:
  - Estadisticas conectadas a la base de datos
  - Filtrado dinamico de solicitudes por estado

body:
## Summary
- Set up Vitest testing framework with React Testing Library
- Added comprehensive test coverage for authentication flow including error handling
- Implemented robust authentication error handling with user-friendly UX
- **Fixed critical authentication bugs** preventing proper error handling and state management
- All tests passing (32 total including error handling scenarios)

## Major Changes

### Testing Infrastructure
- Installed testing dependencies: Vitest, React Testing Library, jsdom
- Created test configuration and centralized mock setup
- Added comprehensive test suites for all auth components

### Authentication Error Handling & Bug Fixes
- **Connection Error Handling**: Proper error states for network/service failures
- **Unified Error UX**: Single "Try Again" button that handles both connection and auth errors
- **Retry Functionality**: Users can retry failed connections with clear feedback
- **🐛 Fixed Connection Retry Bug**: Prevent sign-in attempts when connection retry fails
- **🐛 Fixed User State Bug**: Clear user state when session becomes null (expired sessions)
- **Improved Error Messages**: Actionable guidance with centralized error constants

### Test Coverage Expansion
- **AuthProvider**: 11 comprehensive unit tests covering error scenarios and bug fixes
- **Login Component**: Enhanced tests including bug fix validation and retry functionality
- **useAuth Hook**: Validation tests for error states and retry methods
- **Error Flow Testing**: Complete coverage of connection errors, auth failures, and recovery

## Technical Implementation

### Error Handling Features
- `connectionError` state in AuthProvider for service connectivity issues
- `authActionError` state in Login component for user-initiated auth failures
- `retryAuth` function to allow connection retry attempts
- Automatic error clearing on successful authentication
- Unified error display with context-appropriate messaging

### Bug Fixes Details

#### 1. Connection Retry Bug Fix
**Issue**: `handleGitHubLogin` continued to call `signInWithGitHub()` even when `retryAuth()` failed
**Fix**: Check `connectionError` state after retry attempt; abort sign-in if error persists
**Test**: Added test verifying `signInWithGitHub` is not called when retry fails

#### 2. User State Clearing Bug Fix  
**Issue**: `getSession()` didn't clear user state when session was null, causing stale user data
**Fix**: Added `else` branch to clear user state, matching `onAuthStateChange` behavior
**Test**: Added test verifying user state is cleared on initial load with no session

### Testing Approach
- Unit tests with mocked Supabase dependencies using `as any` for type flexibility
- Comprehensive error scenario coverage (network failures, OAuth errors, timeouts)
- State transition testing for loading/error/success flows
- User interaction testing for retry and error recovery
- **Bug regression testing** to ensure fixes work correctly

## Test Coverage Details
- ✅ Component rendering and children
- ✅ Auth context provider functionality  
- ✅ Loading and error states
- ✅ Connection error handling with retry
- ✅ Authentication method error handling
- ✅ Error state clearing and recovery
- ✅ User state management across error scenarios
- ✅ Connection retry failure handling (bug fix)
- ✅ User state clearing on null sessions (bug fix)
- ✅ Hook usage validation
- ✅ UI state transitions and error display
- ✅ Retry functionality and user guidance

## Test Plan
- [x] Run `npm test` to verify all 32 tests pass
- [x] Test connection error scenarios (network issues)
- [x] Test authentication errors (OAuth failures)
- [x] Verify error recovery and retry functionality
- [x] Test bug fixes: retry failure handling and user state clearing
- [x] Confirm error messaging is user-friendly and actionable
- [x] Ensure no implementation details are tested
- [x] Validate mocks don't interfere with actual functionality

body:
This PR updates [coverage](https://pypi.org/project/coverage) from **6.3.2** to **7.13.0**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 7.13.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Feature: coverage.py now supports :file:`.coveragerc.toml` configuration
  files. These files use TOML syntax and take priority over
  :file:`pyproject.toml` but lower priority than :file:`.coveragerc` files.
  Closes `issue 1643`_ thanks to `Olena Yefymenko <pull 1952_>`_.

- Fix: we now include a permanent .pth file which is installed with the code,
  fixing `issue 2084`_.  In 7.12.1b1 this was done incorrectly: it didn't work
  when using the source wheel (``py3-none-any``).  This is now fixed. Thanks,
  `Henry Schreiner <pull 2100_>`_.

- Deprecated: when coverage.py is installed, it creates three command entry
  points: ``coverage``, ``coverage3``, and ``coverage-3.10`` (if installed for
  Python 3.10). The second and third of these are not needed and will
  eventually be removed. They still work for now, but print a message about
  their deprecation.

.. _issue 1643: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1643
.. _pull 1952: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1952
.. _pull 2100: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2100


.. _changes_7-12-1b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.12.1b1
   ```
   -----------------------------

- Fix: coverage.py now includes a permanent .pth file in the distribution which
  is installed with the code. This fixes `issue 2084`_: failure to patch for
  subprocess measurement when site-packages is not writable.

.. _issue 2084: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2084


.. _changes_7-12-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.12.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- The HTML report now shows separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, as well as the usual combined coverage percentage. Thanks to Ryuta
  Otsuka for the `discussion <issue 2081_>`_ and the `implementation
  <pull 2085_>`_.

- The JSON report now includes separate coverage totals for statements and
  branches, thanks to `Ryuta Otsuka <pull 2090_>`_.

- Fix: ``except*`` clauses were not handled properly under the "sysmon"
  measurement core, causing KeyError exceptions as described in `issue 2086`_.
  This is now fixed.

- Fix: we now defend against aggressive mocking of ``open()`` that could cause
  errors inside coverage.py.  An example of a failure is in `issue 2083`_.

- Fix: in unusual cases where a test suite intentionally exhausts the system's
  file descriptors to test handling errors in ``open()``, coverage.py would
  fail when trying to open source files, as described in `issue 2091`_.  This
  is now fixed.

- A small tweak to the HTML report: file paths now use thin spaces around
  slashes to make them easier to read.

.. _issue 2081: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2081
.. _issue 2083: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2083
.. _pull 2085: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2085
.. _issue 2086: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2086
.. _pull 2090: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2090
.. _issue 2091: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2091


.. _changes_7-11-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the 7.11.1 changes meant that conflicts between a requested measurement
  core and other settings would raise an error. This was a breaking change from
  previous behavior, as reported in `issue 2076`_ and `issue 2078`_.

  The previous behavior has been restored: when the requested core conflicts
  with other settings, another core is used instead, and a warning is issued.

- For contributors: the repo has moved from Ned's `nedbat GitHub account`_ to
  the `coveragepy GitHub organization`_. The default branch has changed from
  master to main.

.. _issue 2076: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2076
.. _issue 2078: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2078
.. _nedbat GitHub account: https://github.com/nedbat
.. _coveragepy GitHub organization: https://github.com/coveragepy


.. _changes_7-11-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: using the "sysmon" measurement core in 7.11.1, if Python code was
  claimed to come from a non-Python file, a ``NotPython`` exception could be
  raised. This could happen for example with Jinja templates compiled to
  Python, as reported in `issue 2077`_. This is now fixed.

- Doc: corrected the first entry in the 7.11.1 changelog.

.. _issue 2077: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2077


.. _changes_7-11-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: some chanages to details of how the measurement core is chosen, and how
  conflicting settings are handled. The "sysmon" core cannot be used with some
  conurrency settings, with dynamic context, and in Python 3.12/3.13, with
  branch measurement.

  - If the core is not specified and defaults to "sysmon" (Python 3.14+), but
    other settings conflict with sysmon, then the "ctrace" core will be used
    instead with no warning. For concurrency conflicts, this used to produce an
    error, as described in `issue 2064`_.

  - If the "sysmon" core is explicitly requested in your configuration, but
    other settings conflict, an error is now raised. This used to produce a
    warning.

- Fix: some multi-line case clauses or for loops (and probably other
  constructs) could cause incorrect claims of missing branches with the
  sys.monitoring core, as described in `issue 2070`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: when running in pytest under coverage, a ``breakpoint()`` would stop in
  the wrong frame, one level down from where it should, as described in `issue
  1420`_. This was due to a coverage change in v6.4.1 that seemed to give a
  slight performance improvement, but I couldn't reproduce the performance
  gain, so it's been reverted, fixing the debugger problem.

- A new debug option ``--debug=core`` shows which core is in use and why.

- Split ``sqlite`` debugging information out of the ``sys`` :ref:`coverage
  debug <cmd_debug>` and :ref:`cmd_run_debug` options since it's bulky and not
  very useful.

- Updated the :ref:`howitworks` page to better describe the three different
  measurement cores.

.. _issue 1420: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1420
.. _issue 2064: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2064
.. _issue 2070: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2070


.. _changes_7-11-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.11.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Dropped support for Python 3.9, declared support for Python 3.15 alpha.


.. _changes_7-10-7:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.10.7
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Performance: with branch coverage in large files, generating HTML, JSON, or
  LCOV reports could take far too long due to some quadratic behavior when
  creating the function and class index pages.  This is now fixed, closing
  `issue 2048`_.  Thanks to Daniel Diniz for help diagnosing the problem.

- Most warnings and a few errors now have links to a page in the docs

.. _issue 1921: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1921
.. _issue 2048: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2048

- Fix: ``source`` directories were not properly communicated to subprocesses

    PRIMARY KEY (vec_id)
);

author: rpschoenburg
body:
Fixes the workspace add deadlock issue.

For context, in the old iteration of parallel_batched_small_file_upload, I was using a semaphore to limit the number of outbound files on the server. This definitely was working at one point, but I'd since ran into a deadlock with consistently whereby the semaphore would never actually release its permits, getting the function stuck after the permits ran out.

This PR rebuilds that function from the ground up, simplifying the logic drastically. We now:
1. Split the small files into batches of ~AVG_CHUNK_SIZE
2. Spawn a producer tasks, which uses futures::stream with the file batches to move each batch into a blocking threadpool (tokio::task::spawn_blocking) and process them in parallel. When each batch is completed, it is sent into the mpsc pipeline
3. Spawn a consumer task, which uses tokio_stream::ReceiverStream to read from the mpsc pipeline, and creates an upload task for each read batch.
4. Collect the errors and err_files from this operation, and retry the err_files. If there are errors with the operations as a whole, or any files fail to upload after retry, return Err. Otherwise, return successfully.

There still isn't directly any retry functionality for the version file upload. That's definetly the next step here. However, this branch solves the deadlock issue by not using a semaphore while maintaining the performance benefits from the initial optimization.

To test:

1. Create a large dataset of small files. This PR doesn't relate to the large file upload at all
2. Create a remote, locally or otherwise, and create a workspace on that remote
3. Use `oxen workspace add` on the dataset as a whole. The expected behavior is for files to be processed and uploaded continuously, so long as there's still room in the upload pipeline. No files should fail after retry

Consider using different kinds of files, or otherwise different small file workloads. The directory structure shouldn't be relevant to this logic, as dirs aren't directly uploaded to workspaces

OCaml requires type names to be lowercase while Standard ML allows any capitalization. Constructors remain uppercase in both.

## Changes

Updated Delphin module type definitions:
- **Type names**: `Decs` → `decs`, `CreateDecl` → `createDecl`, `FormDecl` → `formDecl`, `FunDecl` → `funDecl`, `ValDecl` → `valDecl`, `Cases` → `cases`, `World` → `world`, `Form` → `form`, `Prog` → `prog`, `Head` → `head`, `Pat` → `pat`, `MDec` → `mDec`, `Block` → `block`, `Term` → `term`, `Dec` → `dec`
- **Constructors**: Remain uppercase (e.g., `Empty`, `FunDecl`, `Create`, `Decs`)

## Example

```ocaml
(* Before *)
and Decs 
  = Empty
  | FunDecl of FunDecl * Decs

(* After *)
and decs 
  = Empty
  | FunDecl of funDecl * decs
```

## Files Modified
- `lib/delphin/dextsyn.ml` - type definitions
- `lib/delphin/dextsyn.mli` - type signatures  
- `lib/delphin/trans.mli` - type references

body:
### What problem does this PR solve?

Currently this variable is only used in DCHECK. Whether to apply the const optimization (is_const_and_have_executed) does not depend on this variable.

```
    bool is_const_and_have_executed() const {
        return (is_constant() && (_constant_col != nullptr));
    }
```

We can determine whether we're currently executing a constant expression by checking if block is nullptr.

get_const_col no longer constructs a block

```
    int result = -1;
    Block block;
    // If block is empty, some functions will produce no result. So we insert a column with
    // single value here.
    block.insert({ColumnUInt8::create(1), std::make_shared<DataTypeUInt8>(), ""});

    RETURN_IF_ERROR(execute(context, &block, &result));
```

now

```
    ColumnPtr result;
    RETURN_IF_ERROR(execute_column(context, nullptr, 1, result));
    _constant_col = std::make_shared<ColumnPtrWrapper>(result);
```

author: zailiwang
body:
The previous `run_cpu.py` assumed that the CPU cores were always evenly distributed among the sub-numa nodes. However, in some recent Xeon SKUs, the assumption does not hold. The current script would not be functioning well in `--throughput-mode` or `--latency-mode` since cross-numa cores are assigned to the respective instances due that the imbalance of the core distribution is not well handled.

In this PR, this issue is resolved by expanding the input param number of `--ncore-per-instance` argument. For instance, if the core distribution of the sub-numa nodes is 43-43-42, we can specify `--ncore-per-instance 43 43 42` so that the cores of the initiated instances are aligned with the core distributions. The logic for `--throughput-mode` and `--latency-mode` are updated correspondingly. The logics are updated also to ensure backward compatibility, setting a single param (e.g. `--ncore-per-instance 4`) would take the same effect as before.

This work was originated from #133835 , in which a lot features were mixed, so extract only the most useful functionality into this PR.

author: copilot
body:
Defines a strongly-typed wire protocol for streaming multimodal data (audio, video, IMU) from Ray-Ban Meta glasses via Android DAT client to the Python backend.

## Implementation

### Schema Definition
- **JSON Schema** (`schemas/dat_wire_protocol.json`): 8 message types with validation rules
  - `SessionInitRequest/Response`: Device capabilities negotiation
  - `StreamChunk`: Unified envelope for audio/frame/IMU with type-specific metadata
  - `TurnCompleteRequest/Response`: Agent query finalization with action list
  - `ErrorResponse`: Standardized error codes

### Python Models
- **Pydantic models** (`src/wire/dat_protocol.py`): Type-safe request/response classes
  - Field validators for sample rates, formats, sensor types
  - `AudioMeta`, `FrameMeta`, `ImuMeta` discriminated by chunk type
  - Python 3.8+ compatible (uses `List[T]` not `list[T]`)

### FastAPI Endpoints
- **`POST /dat/session`**: Initialize streaming session, returns UUID
- **`POST /dat/stream`**: Buffer chunks in `_DAT_REGISTRY` with payload size validation (10MB limit)
- **`POST /dat/turn/complete`**: Process buffered data and return agent response (business logic TODO)

### Android Integration
- Complete Kotlin data class definitions with Moshi adapters
- `DatWireProtocolClient` implementation using OkHttp
- Integration examples with `DatSmartGlassController`

## Protocol Flow

```kotlin
// Android client
val client = DatWireProtocolClient("http://backend:8000")

// 1. Initialize session
val session = client.initSession(deviceId = "rayban-meta-12345")

// 2. Stream data chunks
client.sendAudioChunk(session.sessionId, sequenceNumber++, audioData, 16000)
client.sendFrameChunk(session.sessionId, sequenceNumber++, jpegData, 1920, 1080)

// 3. Get agent response
val result = client.completeTurn(session.sessionId)
result.actions.forEach { executeAction(it) }
```

## Design Decisions

- **Base64 encoding**: JSON-compatible binary payloads, 33% overhead acceptable for 1MB chunks
- **Sequence numbers + timestamps**: Out-of-order detection and debugging
- **Turn-based processing**: Aligns with conversational AI pattern, clear buffer boundaries
- **Extensible metadata**: Union types enable adding sensor types without breaking changes

## Testing

27 tests covering validation, serialization, error handling. Uses importlib to avoid loading heavy dependencies (whisper, torch) during test collection.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> Wire protocol & session management (Shared)
> 
> Prompt 7 – Define the Android ↔ Python wire schema
> 
> Goal: Make the “E2E handshake” between mobile and backend explicit and strongly typed.
> 
> We want to formalize the wire protocol between the Android DAT client and the SmartGlass-AI-Agent Python backend.
> 
> Context:
> - The backend already has some JSON shapes (requests/responses) for multimodal queries and responds with `response` + `actions`.
> - We now have streaming audio and frames from Ray-Ban glasses via the mobile app, and we want sessions to be robust and debuggable.
> 
> Task:
> 1. Create a new file `schemas/datat_wire_protocol.json` (or similar) that defines:
>    - A `SessionInitRequest` / `SessionInitResponse`.
>    - A `StreamChunk` envelope with:
>      - `session_id`
>      - `chunk_type` (`audio` | `frame`)
>      - `timestamp_ms`
>      - `payload` (base64-encoded bytes)
>      - Optional `meta` (e.g., frame size, sample rate).
>    - A `TurnCompleteRequest` / `TurnCompleteResponse` that wraps the agent’s NLG result and actions.
> 2. In Python, add Pydantic (or dataclasses + validation functions) types for these schemas in a new `src/wire/dat_protocol.py`.
> 3. Sketch (or partially implement) FastAPI/Flask endpoints:
>    - `POST /dat/session`
>    - `POST /dat/stream`
>    - `POST /dat/turn/complete`
>    With TODO markers where business logic needs to be filled in.
> 
> Please:
> - Ensure the types are easy to consume from Android (Kotlin data classes).
> - Make the protocol extensible for future sensor types (e.g., IMU) with minimal changes.


</details>

author: bobboli
body:
## Description
This PR adds support for Skip Softmax Attention, as described in [https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12087](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.12087), which is a add-on feature for FlashAttention style kernels that allows dynamic sparse attention.
- On Hopper, the implementation is integrated into `fmha_v2` for prefilling. 
- On Blackwell, the feature supported by Trtllm-Gen kernels for both prefilling and decoding (provided as cubins).
- Add 3rd Sparse Attention algorithm, `skip_softmax`, and provide necessary runtime modifications.

### Anticipated API:
Through LLM API:
``` python
from tensorrt_llm import LLM
from tensorrt_llm.llmapi import SkipSoftmaxAttentionConfig
sparse_attention_config = SkipSoftmaxAttentionConfig(threshold_scale_factor=1000.0)
# Additionally, the threshold_scale_factor for prefill and decode could be separately configured.
sparse_attention_config = SkipSoftmaxAttentionConfig(threshold_scale_factor={"prefill": 1000.0, "decode": 500.0})
llm = LLM(
   model="Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507",
   sparse_attention_config=sparse_attention_config,
   # Other LLM arguments...
)
```

Through YAML config:
``` bash
cat >extra_llm_api_options.yaml <<EOF
sparse_attention_config:
    algorithm: skip_softmax
    threshold_scale_factor: 1000.0
EOF

# Additionally, the threshold_scale_factor for prefill and decode could be separately configured.
cat >extra_llm_api_options.yaml <<EOF
sparse_attention_config:
    algorithm: skip_softmax
    threshold_scale_factor: 
        prefill: 1000.0
        decode: 500.0
EOF

trtllm-serve Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 --extra_llm_api_options extra_llm_api_options.yaml
```


### Known issues:
- `fmha_v2` FP8 + Skip Softmax attention has accuracy issues.
- `XQA` based decoding on Hopper has not been integrated yet.

body:
## Summary

This PR adds a new `dotenv` input type that reads secrets directly from `.env` files, eliminating the need to manually `source .env` before running `pouch retrieve`.

### Features
- New `dotenv` input type with optional `filePath` parameter (defaults to `.env`)
- Variable interpolation support (`${VAR}` syntax)
- Multi-line values using heredoc syntax (`"""` or `'''`)
- Comprehensive unit tests including an integration test

### Usage

```yaml
keys:
  - API_KEY
  - DATABASE_URL

input:
  type: dotenv
  filePath: ./.env  # optional, defaults to .env

outputs:
  - filePath: ./Secrets.swift
    typeName: Secrets
```

### Example `.env` file

```env
# Comments are supported
API_KEY=secret123

# Variable interpolation
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_CONNECTION=${DB_HOST}:${DB_PORT}

# Multi-line values
PRIVATE_KEY="""
-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
MIIEpAIBAAKCAQEAw...
-----END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----
"""
```

Closes #7

author: sanity
body:
## Problem

The `test_three_node_network_connectivity` test was flaky due to PUT forward messages being lost during NAT routing. The issue manifested as:

1. Message successfully queued to channel via `peer_connection.sender.send()`
2. Log shows "Message successfully sent to peer connection via explicit address"
3. **But the message never arrives at the receiver**
4. Other messages sent milliseconds later DO arrive
5. Transaction times out

## Root Cause

The `peer_connection_listener` task uses `tokio::select!` to wait on:
- `rx.recv()` - outbound messages from the channel to send
- `conn.recv()` - inbound messages from the network

When a transport error occurs on `conn.recv()`:
1. The error branch is selected (randomly, since select is unbiased by default)
2. The task logs the error and immediately exits
3. The `rx` receiver is dropped
4. **Any pending outbound messages in the channel are lost**

This is a classic race condition where messages can be queued to the channel but never processed because the listener exits before draining them.

## Solution

Two changes to fix the race:

1. **Add `biased;` to the select!** - This ensures the outbound channel is checked first on each iteration, reducing the window where messages can be lost

2. **Add `drain_pending_messages()`** - Before terminating on transport errors, attempt to send any queued outbound messages. Even if the connection is degraded, some messages may still succeed.

## Testing

- Test passes consistently in local runs
- The fix is defensive - it attempts to process messages but gracefully handles failures during drain

## Impact

This should unblock PRs with red CI due to this flaky test (#2246, #2251, #2252).

Fixes #2253

body:
jQuery UI datepickers displayed incorrectly when using `numberOfMonths > 1` or `inline: true` options. Missing CSS caused overlapping months and missing borders.

## Changes

**Inline datepicker support**
- Added `.ui-datepicker-inline` styles with top border and `inline-block` display

**Multi-month layout**
- Added `.ui-datepicker-multi` container with auto-width
- 8px spacing between adjacent month groups via adjacent sibling selector
- Removed inner borders on `.ui-datepicker-group-first/last/middle` headers for seamless appearance

## Example

```javascript
// Both configurations now render correctly
$("#date").datepicker({ numberOfMonths: 2 });
$("#inline").datepicker({ inline: true });
```

All changes in `src/general.scss`, compiled to `datepicker.css` and `datepicker.min.css`.

body:
## 概要と理由
issue-147で計画されていたRules UIのリファクタリングを完成させました。issue-147完了前にインフラやアーキテクチャに変更があったため、その成果と理念を受け継ぎ、Clean ArchitectureとAtomic Design原則に従ってRulesAppコンポーネント群を再構築しました。

## 主な変更点

### 1. Atomic Design構造でのコンポーネント分離
- **Organism層**: 
  - `RulesTable`: ルール一覧テーブル表示
  - `EmptyStateMessage`: ルール未登録時のメッセージ表示
- **Molecule層**:
  - `RuleTableRow`: 個別ルール行の表示
  - `LoadingMessage`: 読み込み中メッセージ
  - `ErrorMessage`: エラーメッセージ表示

### 2. Clean Architecture原則の適用
- RulesApp.tsxを適切にリファクタリングし、UseCase経由でのデータ取得に統一
- コンポーネント間の依存関係をClean Architecture層に準拠して整理

### 3. CSS ModulesとUI設計の統一化
- CSS Modulesを使用した一貫性のあるスタイリング
- E2Eテスト用のdata-testid属性の追加
- 正規表現バッジ機能の完全削除（設計仕様書との整合性確保）

### 4. Storybookによるコンポーネント文書化
- 分割した全コンポーネントのStory作成
- 各状態（ローディング、エラー、空状態、正常状態）のパターン網羅

### 5. 包括的なテスト対応
- 既存テスト（Unit Tests: 322テスト、E2E Tests: 12テスト）の全維持
- CSS Modules統一に伴うテスト調整
- data-testidベースのE2Eテスト実装によるテスト安定性向上

## テスト方法
[動作確認の手順]
- `make testlint` で回帰テスト通過を確認
  - Unit Tests: 77ファイル、322テスト - 全て成功
  - E2E Tests: 12テスト - 全て成功  
  - TypeScript Compilation: エラーなし
  - ESLint: エラーなし
  - Unused Code Detection: 未使用コードなし

## 補足
- 9回のスクラムイテレーションを通じて段階的に品質向上を実現
- CSS Modulesの統一的なアプローチにより保守性を向上
- E2Eテストの安定性向上のためdata-testid属性を導入
- issue-147の成果と理念を継承しつつ、最新のアーキテクチャに適応した実装

## 本スコープの対象外となったタスク
なし（全タスク完了済み）

body:
Users had to switch to Django admin panel to create, edit, or delete bookings. This adds inline CRUD operations directly in the account detail view.

## Changes

### Backend
- **Views** (`core/views.py`): Added `booking_create`, `booking_update`, `booking_delete` with validation and transfer protection
- **URLs** (`core/urls.py`): Registered routes for `/accounts/<id>/bookings/create/`, `/bookings/<id>/update/`, `/bookings/<id>/delete/`
- **Tests** (`core/tests.py`): Added `BookingCRUDViewTest` class with 9 tests covering create, update, delete operations and edge cases

### Frontend
- **Modals** (`account_detail.html`): Replaced placeholder with functional create/edit/delete modals using Bootstrap
- **Actions**: Added edit (pencil) and delete (trash) buttons to each booking row
- **JS**: Implemented `openEditModal` and `openDeleteModal` functions to populate forms with booking data

## Implementation Details

Forms require `booking_date` and `amount`; `category`, `payee`, and `status` are optional. Transfer bookings cannot be deleted individually (validation enforced server-side).

After successful operations, users are redirected to the correct month view with success messages.

<details>

### [`v7.1.5`](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/releases/tag/v7.1.5): 🌈 allow setting `cache-local-path` without `enable-cache: true`

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/compare/v7.1.4...v7.1.5)

#### Changes

[#​612](https://redirect.github.com/astral-sh/setup-uv/pull/612) fixed a faulty behavior where this action set `UV_CACHE_DIR` even though `enable-cache` was `false`. It also fixed the cases were the cache dir is already configured in a settings file like `pyproject.toml` or `UV_CACHE_DIR` was already set.  Here the action shouldn't overwrite or set `UV_CACHE_DIR`.

These fixes introduced an unwanted behavior: You can still set `cache-local-path` but this action didn't do anything. This release fixes that.

You can now use `cache-local-path` to automatically set `UV_CACHE_DIR` even when `enable-cache` is `false` (or gets set to false by default e.g. on self-hosted runners)

```yaml
- name: This is now possible
  uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
  with:
    enable-cache: false
    cache-local-path: "/path/to/cache"
```

Implements snapshot testing for `gh aw add` to detect unintentional changes to generated workflow scaffolding.

## Implementation

- **Test infrastructure** - 4 test cases covering: basic addition, custom naming (`-n`), subdirectory placement (`--dir`), numbered copies (`-c`)
- **Normalization** - Filters timestamps, versions, and commit SHAs from comparisons to ensure stability across environments
- **Golden files** - Captures both markdown (`.md`) and compiled YAML (`.lock.yml`) outputs in `pkg/cli/testdata/add_golden/`

# Run tests
go test -v -tags 'integration' -run='^TestAddCommandGolden$' ./pkg/cli

# Update snapshots after intentional changes
UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 go test -v -tags 'integration' -run='^TestAddCommandGolden$' ./pkg/cli

author: copilot
body:
Implements production-ready hardware wallet integration for Ledger Nano S/X and Trezor Model One/T devices with BIP44 derivation path `m/44'/9999'/0'/0/n`.

## Architecture

Refactored `hardware.rs` into modular structure:

- **`hardware/mod.rs`** - `HardwareWalletDevice` trait, `HardwareWallet` manager, `SigningMethod` enum (SW/HW abstraction)
- **`hardware/ledger.rs`** - Full APDU protocol (0x02 GET_PUBLIC_KEY, 0x04 SIGN, 0x06 GET_APP_CONFIG) over USB HID
- **`hardware/trezor.rs`** - USB HID connection, BIP44 parsing, passphrase support (protobuf messages placeholder)
- **`hardware/mock.rs`** - Test device for CI/CD

## Implementation

**Ledger Integration:**
- APDU command serialization with BIP44 path encoding (hardened indices marked 0x8000_0000)
- Device confirmation required for all signing operations
- Firmware version and app verification
- Multi-chain address derivation (BitCell/BTC/ETH)

**Trezor Integration:**
- HID transport layer ready
- Passphrase support for hidden wallets via `.with_passphrase()`
- Protocol structure complete (needs protobuf implementation for production)

**BIP44 Paths:**
- BitCell: coin type 9999
- Bitcoin: coin type 0
- Ethereum: coin type 60

## Usage

```rust
use bitcell_wallet::{HardwareWallet, HardwareWalletType, Chain};

// Connect and derive BitCell address
let hw = HardwareWallet::connect(HardwareWalletType::Ledger)?
    .with_derivation_path("m/44'/9999'/0'/0/0");
let address = hw.get_address(Chain::BitCell)?;

// Sign transaction (requires device confirmation)
let signed = hw.sign_transaction(&tx)?;

// Unified interface
let method = SigningMethod::Hardware(hw);
let signed = method.sign(&tx)?;
```

## Testing

- 17 new hardware wallet integration tests
- Mock device enables CI/CD without physical hardware
- Features: `--features ledger,trezor`

## Security

- Private keys never leave secure element
- Physical confirmation mandatory for signing
- Derivation paths displayed on device
- Error handling for device disconnection, user rejection, wrong app

## Limitations

- Trezor requires protobuf protocol completion for production use
- Physical device testing pending (software complete)
- Ledger BitCell app not published (falls back to Ethereum app)

## Documentation

- `docs/HARDWARE_WALLET_GUIDE.md` - Setup, usage, troubleshooting (481 lines)
- `docs/HARDWARE_WALLET_IMPLEMENTATION.md` - Technical details (480 lines)

The semantic-release change-detector plugin lacked test coverage and practical guidance for adoption.

## Tests Added (46 new, 86 total)

**Integration tests** - Complete lifecycle validation across all operating modes:
- Validate mode: mismatch detection, over-bumping, `failOnMismatch` behavior
- Override mode: API-driven versioning, new package handling, null returns for no changes
- Advisory mode: non-blocking warnings, missing file tolerance

**Edge cases** - Declaration file discovery, git baseline resolution, error handling:
- File discovery: symlinks, scoped packages, fallback locations, explicit/relative paths
- Git operations: branch fallbacks (main/master/HEAD~1), tag verification, custom refs
- Error scenarios: missing files, new packages without history, temp directory cleanup

## Documentation Added

**Troubleshooting** - 5 common failure modes with solutions:
- Declaration file not found → build ordering, explicit paths, package.json types field
- Version mismatch errors → commit message fixes, mode selection
- CI/CD issues → fetch-depth, tag availability

**Common Pitfalls** - 6 real-world configuration mistakes:
- Build ordering, plugin sequence, shallow clones, internal vs public APIs

**FAQ** - 10 questions covering JavaScript projects, monorepos, migration strategies, customization

**Advanced Examples** - 6 configuration scenarios: monorepo setup, API Extractor integration, strict validation, gradual adoption, custom baselines, private packages

Example new test pattern:
```typescript
it('completes full lifecycle with matching version bump', async () => {
  // Setup with git tag baseline
  initGitRepo(project.baseDir)
  createGitTag(project.baseDir, 'v1.0.0')
  
  // API change: add new function (minor)
  fs.writeFileSync(declarationFile, addedFunction)

  analyzeCommits({}, context)
  verifyRelease({}, context)  // Validates bump matches changes

  expect(notes).toContain('Added Exports')
})
```

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR refactors the `imixv2` implant to address readability and maintainability concerns. The primary changes involve modularizing the large `shell.rs` file into a structured directory and introducing helper methods in `agent.rs`, `main.rs`, and `task.rs` to reduce nesting and code duplication.

### Key Changes
*   **Modularization**: `implants/imixv2/src/shell.rs` has been split into `implants/imixv2/src/shell/` containing:
    *   `pty.rs`: Logic for spawning and managing PTY processes.
    *   `repl.rs`: Logic for the REPL loop and agent integration.
    *   `parser.rs`: The VT100/ANSI input parser.
    *   `terminal.rs`: Output rendering and terminal manipulation.
*   **Agent Refactoring**: `implants/imixv2/src/agent.rs` now uses `with_transport` and `spawn_subtask` helpers to handle common transport acquisition and async spawning patterns, cleaner `Agent` trait implementation.
*   **Main Loop Simplification**: `implants/imixv2/src/main.rs` loop body extracted to `run_agent_cycle`.
*   **Task Execution**: `implants/imixv2/src/task.rs` breaks down the `spawn` method into distinct setup, execution, and reporting phases.

### verification
*   `cargo check` passes.
*   `cargo test` passes.
*   Refactoring verified to preserve original logic flow.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body:
This PR replaces the Python-based `biotite` parser for PDB and mmCIF files with a Rust implementation using the `pdbtbx` crate. This significantly improves parsing performance for large structures. The Rust extension (`priox_rust`) is wrapped in `src/priox/io/parsing/rust.py` which converts the raw data into `biotite.structure.AtomArray` objects, preserving full compatibility with the existing pipeline (including Hydride integration). Tests verify correctness for both PDB and mmCIF formats. Trajectory parsing (XTC/DCD) currently remains with `mdtraj` (C++) as `pdbtbx` does not support these formats, but the architecture allows for future Rust implementation.

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

author: jaseemjaskp
body:
## Summary
Skip CI steps that require secrets or write permissions for forked PRs to prevent workflow failures.

## Changes
- **ci-test.yaml**: Skip PR comment step for fork PRs (sticky-pull-request-comment requires write access)
- **ci-container-build.yaml**: Skip Docker Hub login for fork PRs (secrets not available to forks)

## Why
Forked PRs don't have access to repository secrets and can't write comments to PRs, causing these steps to fail. This change allows the rest of the CI to run successfully for external contributors.

body: ## Description This PR establishes the foundational architecture for a multi-tenant, white-labeled, no-code front-end configuration layer for Settler.dev. It introduces the core data models, tenant resolution logic, dynamic theming, and a block-based page rendering system. This work lays the groundwork for future features like the Site Designer UI and A/B testing. ## Type of Change - [x] Feature - [ ] Bug Fix - [ ] Integration - [ ] Infrastructure - [ ] Documentation - [ ] Other ## Testing - [ ] Unit tests added/updated - [ ] Integration tests added/updated - [x] Manual testing completed (Core logic and components have been developed, but comprehensive manual testing of the integrated system and UI is pending the implementation of the Site Designer.) ## Checklist - [x] Code follows style guidelines - [x] Self-review completed - [x] Comments added for complex code - [x] Documentation updated - [ ] No new warnings generated - [ ] Tests pass locally - [x] TypeScript types are correct ## Related Issues Closes # ## Screenshots (if applicable) ## Additional Notes This PR completes Steps 1-4 of the multi-tenant site builder task: - **Step 1 (Discovery)**: Documented existing front-end architecture in `docs/frontend-architecture.md`. - **Step 2 (Data Model)**: Added Prisma models for `Tenant`, `TenantBranding`, `TenantNavigation`, `TenantPage`, `TenantPageRevision`, `Experiment`, `ExperimentVariant`, and `ExperimentMetricEvent`, along with a migration. - **Step 3 (Tenant Resolution & Theming)**: Implemented domain/subdomain/path-based tenant resolution, a `TenantThemeProvider` for dynamic branding, and a `TenantNavigation` component. - **Step 4 (Page Schema & Rendering)**: Defined a type-safe block schema (`pageSchema.ts`) and a `PageRenderer.tsx` with 10 initial block components. ## Summary

Add format-agnostic `execution_files` field to manifest that provides explicit paths for Core to use, eliminating directory guessing.

### Changes

- Add `ExecutionFile` struct to `types/manifest.go` with path, format, type fields
- Add `ExecutionFiles` slice to `Format` struct
- Add `populateExecutionFiles()` in `commands.go` to discover files after install
- Support ONNX, GGUF, TFLite, CoreML formats
- Handle multi-encoder models (seq2seq, CLIP) with proper type detection

### Manifest Example

The `execution_files` field in `manifest.yaml` now looks like:

```yaml
spec:
  format:
    type: onnx
    execution_format: onnx
    execution_files:
      - path: onnx/model.onnx
        format: onnx
        type: single
      - path: onnx/model_O1.onnx
        format: onnx
        type: single
```

### Benefits

- **Eliminates path guessing**: Core reads paths directly from manifest
- **Format agnostic**: Works with ONNX, GGUF, TFLite, CoreML
- **Multi-encoder support**: Properly identifies encoder/decoder roles
- **Fixes CI failures**: Models like sentence-transformers with ONNX in onnx/ subdirectory now work

### Testing

- Verified with sentence-transformers model
- All existing tests pass
- Builds successfully

Resolves: #49

author: pichardescu
body:
When storing binary attachments via session.saveChanges(), Buffer data passed directly to FormData.append() was being treated as text, causing LF (0x0A) bytes to be converted to CRLF (0x0D 0x0A) on Windows.

The fix wraps the payload in a Blob with 'application/octet-stream' content type, consistent with how other binary data is handled elsewhere in the codebase (e.g., DatabaseSmuggler.ts:270).

Fixes binary file corruption affecting ZIP, images, PDFs, and any file containing 0x0A bytes.

Added regression test to verify all 256 byte values (0x00-0xFF) are preserved correctly through attachment storage and retrieval.

Fixes #503

author: zuckjet
body:
Fixes #8906

When users have proxy environment variables set (HTTP_PROXY, HTTPS_PROXY, etc.),
  the local development server fails to start with a "TypeError: fetch failed" error.

  ## Root cause

  - Wrangler detects proxy environment variables and sets a global ProxyAgent
  - Miniflare's InspectorProxyController makes a fetch request to `127.0.0.1`
    to connect to the workerd inspector
  - This local request incorrectly goes through the proxy, which typically
    cannot handle localhost addresses, causing the connection to fail

  ## Solution

  Modified `InspectorProxyController.updateConnection()` to use a dedicated
  `Agent` for the local fetch request, bypassing the global proxy settings.
  Local inspector connections should never be proxied.

author: j0sh
body:
Tracks the last input timestamp and the last output timestamp. Subtracting the input
from the output allows for a continuous measurement of gateway-to-orchestrator latency.

For review convenience, the input changes have been committed separately from the output changes.

[ai/live: Track latest input timestamp](https://github.com/livepeer/go-livepeer/commit/569331c8a0dbdfd88cd8401135225b633e7676c9) 
Do this by attaching a timestamp to each MPEG-TS track. Most of the
changes here are a result of changing the segmenter API to use a new
SegmenterTrack struct that can more easily embed and test additional
fields [1] such as the last input timestamp.

This method allows us to cleanly extract the last input TS while
constructing the MediaState object.

The last input timestamp is stored in the original MPEG-TS 90khz
timebase for now, but converted to seconds before logging and Kafka.

[1] webrtc.TrackRemote is nearly impossible to cleanly mock, so
    make the SegmenterTrack take a RTPTrack so we can drop the
    existing TrackRemote in there alongside any additional fields.

[ai/live: Track latest output timestamp](https://github.com/livepeer/go-livepeer/commit/83eb9d1661b1ad5832e5ff6791532899496345ed) 
Use this to measure gateway-to-orchestrator latency continuously.
Surface this in both logs and Kafka metrics.

Introduce a global `media.OutputStats` to track the last seen MPEG-TS
timestamp per track. Spin up a MPEG-TS reader from the trickle
subscriber and publish each track's timestamp to that. For now, the
OutputStats timebase remains at the original 90khz; for logging and
Kafka it is converted to seconds.

When the track stats are calculated, also pull in the OutputStats.
Since we also have the last input timestamp, we can now measure latency.

body:
The stress tensor output now writes the negative virial scaled by the Hartree-to-eV conversion factor, removing the volume normalization.

## Changes

- **`src/dftd_vasp/plugin.py`**: Updated stress calculation from `res["virial"] * (HARTREE_TO_EV / volume)` to `-res["virial"] * HARTREE_TO_EV` and removed volume computation
- **`tests/test_plugin.py`**: Updated stress reference values for all test cases to match new calculation

## Technical Detail

The stress tensor now has units of eV and sign convention matching the negative virial:

```python
# Before
volume = abs(np.linalg.det(constants.lattice_vectors * ANGSTROM_TO_BOHR))
additions.stress += res["virial"] * (HARTREE_TO_EV / volume)

# After
additions.stress += -res["virial"] * HARTREE_TO_EV
```

This changes stress values from small positive quantities (~10⁻⁵) to larger negative quantities (~10⁻¹) in eV units.

body:
After PR #16 introduced automatic pipe handle disposal to prevent deadlocks, tests are needed to verify that `ProcessHandle.Start` works correctly with named pipes and sockets, not just anonymous pipes.

## Changes

**NamedPipeTests.cs** - 1 test covering:
- Unix: FIFO creation and usage with `ProcessHandle.Start`, verifying handles are recognized as pipes via `IsPipe()`

**SocketTests.cs** - 1 test covering:
- Unix: Socket pairs (`socketpair()`) with `ProcessHandle.Start`, confirming sockets are treated as pipes

All tests use synchronous I/O (no `FileOptions.Asynchronous`) as STD handles typically expect blocking operations. Tests pass handles directly to `ProcessHandle.Start` without shell redirection.

**Note**: Windows named pipe tests were removed due to deadlocking issues that require further investigation.

## Example Usage

```csharp
// Create a Unix socket pair for process output
int[] fds = new int[2];
socketpair(AF_UNIX, SOCK_STREAM, 0, fds);
SafeFileHandle readSocket = new(fds[0], ownsHandle: true);
SafeFileHandle writeSocket = new(fds[1], ownsHandle: true);

// Verify socket is recognized as a pipe
Assert.True(writeSocket.IsPipe());

body:
# Migration from Newtonsoft.Json to System.Text.Json

Complete migration from Newtonsoft.Json to System.Text.Json while maintaining exact backward compatibility with existing JSON format and MessagePack serialization.

## Changes

### Package Dependencies
- Added `NodaTime.Serialization.SystemTextJson` v1.2.0
- Upgraded `System.Text.Json` to v8.0.5 for netstandard2.0/2.1 and net462
- Removed `Flurl.Http.Newtonsoft` (no longer needed)
- **Removed `NodaTime.Serialization.JsonNet`** (completely replaced by STJ)

### New Serialization Infrastructure
- **SystemTextJsonContentSerializer**: Replaces `JsonContentSerializer` in Client.cs
- **Client.CreateDefaultJsonSerializerOptions()**: Internal static method to create configured JsonSerializerOptions (eliminates duplication in tests)
- **DictionaryJsonConverterSTJ**: Custom converter maintains Key/Value array format for complex keys (e.g., `Dictionary<LocalDateTime, double?>`)
  - **Excludes `Dictionary<string, JsonElement>`** to preserve `JsonExtensionData` built-in behavior
- **TimeTransformConverterSTJ**: Polymorphic converter for TimeTransform hierarchy using discriminator property (used via attribute)
- **DerivedCfgBaseConverterSTJ**: STJ-only polymorphic converter for DerivedCfg hierarchy
- **JsonPolymorphicConverter**: Reusable base for polymorphic deserialization

### Deleted Newtonsoft.Json Files
- Removed `JsonContentSerializer.cs`
- Removed `DictionaryJsonConverter.cs`
- Removed `TimeTransformBaseConverter.cs`
- Removed Newtonsoft portion of `DerivedCfgBaseConverter.cs`

### DTO Migration
**Migrated all `[JsonProperty]` attributes to `[JsonPropertyName]`**:
- **AuctionRow**: Short property names (P, N, ID, T, S, D, Q, AD, AQ, BT)
- **AssessmentRow**: Short property names (P, N, ID, PR, T, S, O, C, H, L, VP, VG, VT)
- **TimeSerieRow.Actual**: Short property names (P, C, ID, T, D, S, E)
- **TimeSerieRow.Versioned**: Short property names (P, C, ID, V, T, D, S, E)
- **BidAskRow**: Short property names (P, N, ID, PR, T, BBP, BAP, BBQ, BAQ, LP, LQ)
- **ArtesianSdkProblemDetail**: Migrated to STJ with `[JsonExtensionData]` using `JsonElement`
- **TimeTransformBase**: Removed Newtonsoft using statements
- **DerivedCfgBase**: Removed Newtonsoft using statements

### Configuration
```csharp
// Reusable configuration via internal method
var jsonOptions = Client.CreateDefaultJsonSerializerOptions();
// Returns options configured with:
// - PropertyNamingPolicy = null (PascalCase)
// - DictionaryKeyPolicy = null (Preserve key casing)
// - DefaultIgnoreCondition = WhenWritingNull
// - NumberHandling = AllowNamedFloatingPointLiterals
// - NodaTime converters with Tzdb
// - DictionaryJsonConverterSTJFactory (excludes Dictionary<string, JsonElement>)
// - JsonStringEnumConverter
```

### Test Coverage (26 Serialization Tests)
- **38 original compatibility tests** reduced to **20 tests** (removed redundant serialization tests per review feedback):
  - Dictionaries, polymorphism (TimeTransform, DerivedCfg), null handling, and UpsertData structures
- **5 Row class deserialization-only tests**: Validate short property name deserialization with focus on DateTimeOffset and nullable properties
  - AuctionRow, AssessmentRow, TimeSerieRow.Actual, TimeSerieRow.Versioned, BidAskRow
  - **Fixed TimeSerieRow.Versioned**: Version property correctly uses `DateTime` without timezone offset
  - All DateTimeOffset assertions use "+00:00" format matching JSON
- **2 ProblemDetails tests**: Validate JsonExtensionData functionality with STJ
- **All test methods use literal JSON strings** generated once from Newtonsoft.Json with original master settings (including `NullValueHandling.Ignore`)
- Tests validate:
  - **STJ can deserialize JSON created by Newtonsoft.Json** (backward compatibility)
  - **STJ serializes to equivalent JSON as Newtonsoft.Json** (forward compatibility)
  - Comparison uses `JsonNode.DeepEquals()` with `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive=false`
- Tests reuse `Client.CreateDefaultJsonSerializerOptions()` to avoid configuration duplication
- All Parse calls use `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` explicitly for test reliability
- **All 308 tests passing** (15 manual integration tests skipped)

### JSON Generation Process
- Created temporary JsonLiteralGenerator tool to programmatically generate all JSON literals
- Used Newtonsoft.Json with original master settings + `NullValueHandling.Ignore`
- Generated JSON literal strings for all test scenarios
- Literals embedded as const strings in test file for non-regression validation

## Example JSON Formats (Unchanged)

### Dictionary serialization with complex keys:
```json
[
  {"Key": "2024-01-01T00:00:00", "Value": 100.5},
  {"Key": "2024-01-02T12:30:00", "Value": 101.2}
]
```

### Row classes maintain compact JSON with short property names:
```json
{"P":"TestProvider","N":"TestCurve","ID":100001,"T":"2024-01-01T12:00:00+00:00","S":"Bid","D":50.0}
```

### TimeSerieRow.Versioned with DateTime (no timezone offset):
```json
{"P":"TestProvider","C":"TestCurve","ID":100001,"V":"2024-01-01T10:00:00","T":"2024-01-01T12:00:00+00:00","D":100.5}
```

### ProblemDetails with extension data (flattened properties):
```json
{"type":"validation_error","title":"Validation Failed","status":400,"customField":"customValue"}
```

> 
> Configure the serialization settings with:
> * Add Nodatime STJ Converters with Tzdb
> * Migrate polymorphic custom converters
> * Use PascalCase for property names
> * Do not alter casing for dictionary string keys
> * Null properies should not be present in the serialized
> 
> Take inspiration from https://github.com/ARKlab/Ark.Tools/tree/a991d811f21787154167308b7578cfd285c016f9/Ark.Tools.SystemTextJson but don't take it as a dependency but you can reuse the Polymorphic base converter from there.
> 
> Add serialization tests before migrating by using the current serializer to generate the json strings to be used as input for deser or as expectation for serialization. These tests serve as non-regression.
> Focus tests on objects with Polymorphism and Dictionaries to ensure that custom converters are code-covered. Focus on these:
> * MarketData Entity Tags dictionary
> * Timetransform polymorphic object
> * MarketData Entity DerivedCfg polymorphism
> * UpsertData dictionaries properties (Rows, Assessments, etc.)
> 
> Additionally:
> * Ensure that nulls are skipped and not in the payload
> * Accept that json strings are different as long are equals. Compare using JsonNode.DeepEquals() from STJ 
> 
>

body:
PR comments (fired as issue_comment events) now respect branch filters.

- Add in-memory PR branch cache with timestamp ordering
- Cache populated from PR/review/review_comment events
- API fallback on cache miss via installation Octokit
- Lazy TTL (24h) + delete-on-close for garbage collection
- Support retroactive anchor creation when PR base branch changes

I have fixed the **RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration in tui.py**. The issue was caused by the UI thread iterating over tool_executions while the background agent thread was updating it. I modified the code to iterate over a copy of the dictionary, which is a standard thread-safe pattern for this **scenario**

body:
In case `sshd -T | grep key` returns some lines without spaces Hash creation in communicator.rb failed with ArgumentError "odd number of arguments for Hash".

As only "pubkeyacceptedalgorithms", "pubkeyacceptedkeytypes", "hostkeyalgorithms" are needed, change to ignore lines that have no space.

This fixes error:

```
/home/vyos/tasks/VD-2244-thread-starvation/vagrant/plugins/communicators/ssh/communicator.rb:879:in `[]': odd number of arguments for Has
h (ArgumentError)

        opts = Hash[*list.split("\n").map{|line| line.split(" ", 2)}.flatten]
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        from /home/vyos/tasks/VD-2244-thread-starvation/vagrant/plugins/communicators/ssh/communicator.rb:879:in `supported_key_types'
        from /home/vyos/tasks/VD-2244-thread-starvation/vagrant/plugins/communicators/ssh/communicator.rb:215:in `ready?'
        from /home/vyos/tasks/VD-2244-thread-starvation/vagrant/plugins/communicators/ssh/communicator.rb:91:in `block in wait_for_ready'
        from /home/vyos/.local/share/gem/ruby/3.3.0/gems/timeout-0.5.0/lib/timeout.rb:222:in `block in timeout'
        from /home/vyos/.local/share/gem/ruby/3.3.0/gems/timeout-0.5.0/lib/timeout.rb:38:in `handle_timeout'
        from /home/vyos/.local/share/gem/ruby/3.3.0/gems/timeout-0.5.0/lib/timeout.rb:231:in `timeout'
        from /home/vyos/tasks/VD-2244-thread-starvation/vagrant/plugins/communicators/ssh/communicator.rb:66:in `wait_for_ready'
        from /home/vyos/tasks/VD-2244-thread-starvation/vagrant/lib/vagrant/action/builtin/wait_for_communicator.rb:19:in `block in call'
```

I got it while trying to launch NixOS under Vagrant with https://github.com/nix-community/nixbox.git.

`list` in line 872 of communicator.rb ends with

```
"rekeylimit 0 0\npubkeyauthoptions none\n\e]0;\a"
```

I don't know yet where `\e]0;\a` came from, but anyway I think ignoring lines without spaces here is good idea.

author: rdlabo
body:
This PR introduces Swift Package Manager (SPM) support for the plugin and migrates the iOS implementation to the new structure recommended for Capacitor 7+.

### Overview
- Added `Package.swift` to provide official Swift Package Manager support.
- Migrated all iOS source files into `ios/Sources/AppTrackingTransparencyPlugin`, following the SwiftPM-compatible layout.
- Removed legacy Xcode project files (`Plugin.xcodeproj`, `Plugin.xcworkspace`, schemes, plist files, CocoaPods config, etc.).
- Updated the plugin implementation to adopt `CAPBridgedPlugin` and define `identifier`, `jsName`, and `pluginMethods`.
- Updated tests and imports to match the new module name (`AppTrackingTransparencyPlugin`).
- Updated `package.json`:
  - Pointed `files` entry to new iOS paths.
  - Updated build scripts (`rollup.config.mjs`, Prettier/ESLint/SwiftLint dependencies).
  - Updated Capacitor-related devDependencies to v7-compatible versions.
- Added `.gitignore` / `.eslintignore` entries for SwiftPM build directories.

### Why this change?
Capacitor 7 and 8 recommend distributing native iOS plugins using Swift Package Manager rather than CocoaPods.  
This PR removes Xcode project dependencies and enables a clean, modern, SPM-based installation experience for users.

### Notes
- No API changes for JavaScript users.
- The iOS implementation now builds via SwiftPM, ensuring compatibility with modern Xcode toolchains.

If there's anything you'd like me to adjust, please let me know!

author: trueqbit
body:
Yet another PR with a bit of C++17 hygiene and a few improvements.

### C++17:
* Collapsed nested namespaces, meaning: `namespace sqlite_orm { namespace internal {} }` -> `namespace sqlite_orm::internal {}`. This reduces code intendation, and makes it more obvious (to collaborators) what's part of the public namespace.
**Note**: Because this changes a lot of white spacing it is best to **hide whitespace** for [diff comparison](https://github.com/fnc12/sqlite_orm/pull/1469/files?w=1#diff-6ec8fc411a3160c70a21f477044792080726f74a0bc7d62ddfa30a6388c69bf5).
* Avoided using standard type trait variable templates: As long as we don't require a C++17 Standard Library base line we cannot assume that variable templates are available.

### Improvements:
* Qualified calls to `std::get()`. This function is really widely overloaded, so I consider it good practice in template code to qualify it if called with a tuple.
* Simplified a trait testing for whether an expression is a binary operator.

### Fixes:
* Exported `limit()` that was missed in PR #1336.

author: smileyfish
body:
This pull request refactors how maze tile sprites are rendered in the UI. Instead of having many individual React components for each tile type, it introduces a generic `Sprite` component and a centralized `MazeTile` component with a lookup table for all tile variants. This change greatly simplifies the codebase, reduces duplication, and makes it easier to manage and extend tile rendering logic.

**Sprite rendering refactor:**

* Added a new generic `Sprite` component in `sprites/Sprite.tsx` that handles image rendering, rotation, mirroring, and styling for any sprite asset.
* Added a new `MazeTile` component in `tiles/MazeTile.tsx` that uses a comprehensive lookup table (`TILE_SPRITES`) to map logical tile names to sprite assets and their visual transformations. This replaces the need for separate tile components and centralizes all rendering logic.
* Changed the MazeLayer to use the new files and wrote cleaner code

**Codebase cleanup:**

* Removed individual tile components (`EmptyCell.tsx`, `Connector.tsx`, `DoubleCorner.tsx`, `DoubleWall.tsx`, `DoubleWallStop.tsx`, `SharpDoubleCorner.tsx`, `ShortCorner.tsx`, `SingleCorner.tsx`, `SingleWall.tsx`) that previously handled rendering for each maze tile variant.

body:
Adds a `skeleton/` directory containing offline-first developer tooling and automation, plus a scheduled GitHub Action for repository health monitoring (30-day staleness threshold).

## Structure

**Core Tools** (`skeleton/`)
- `dev_copilot.py` - CLI for template-based code generation and review (local LLM support disabled by default)
- `web_agent_app.py` - Streamlit lab at `:8501` with agent manager, assistant, training, and reminder panels
- `train_agent.py`, `repo_maker.py`, `reminder_panel.py` - Supporting utilities

**Templates** (`skeleton/dev_copilot_templates/`)
- `agent_stub.py`, `metadata.py`, `read_helper.py` - Scaffolding templates with `{{name}}`, `{{class_name}}` placeholders

**Automation** (`skeleton/*.sh`)
- `setup_devcopilot.sh`, `create_repo.sh`, `package_agentpacks.sh`, `git_release.sh`, `start_dev_lab.sh`, `run_tests.sh`
- All executable with proper error handling

**Documentation**
- `README_COPILOT.md`, `AUTOMATION_README.md`, `MIGRATION_GUIDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- `UNIVERSITY_GUIDE.md`, `CLASSROOM_UPGRADE_INTRO.md` - Educational use cases

**GitHub Automation** (repository root)
- `.github/workflows/repo_health_check.yml` - Weekly cron, creates issues for repos inactive 30+ days
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/update_repo.md` - Standardized update issue template
- Labels: `repo-health`, `update-suggested`

## Example Usage

```bash
# Generate agent from template
cd skeleton
python dev_copilot.py generate --template agent_stub --name CustomAgent

# Start web lab
./start_dev_lab.sh  # Opens Streamlit at localhost:8501

# Package agents
./package_agentpacks.sh agents dist/agentpacks 1.0.0
```

## Configuration

**Dev Copilot**: Edit `.devcopilot/config.json` to enable local LLM (requires manual model download)

**Health Check**: Modify cron schedule or staleness threshold in workflow, or delete `.github/workflows/repo_health_check.yml` to disable

## Dependencies

- Python 3.8+
- `requirements.txt`: streamlit, pandas, numpy
- `requirements-devcopilot.txt`: pathlib (LLM libs commented out)

All shell scripts use `set -e` for error handling. Python scripts include proper shebangs.

author: wangke19
body:
Reapply the changes from PR #29074 that were previously reverted, mark both certificate tests as informing so failures don't block CI jobs, and skip the tests on ROSA clusters.

### **Current Skip Pattern:**

  The TLS certificate test currently skips on:
  1. MicroShift - doesn't auto-collect TLS (line 101-102)
  2. HyperShift - doesn't auto-collect TLS (line 105-106)
  3. ROSA - doesn't auto-collect TLS (line 108-109, your recent commit f7b77f2df4)

  **Other Managed Platforms - Analysis:**

  1. ARO (Azure Red Hat OpenShift)
  - Regular ARO: Not hosted control plane, runs like standard OCP → should NOT skip
  - ARO HCP (Hosted Control Plane): This is a HyperShift variant
    - Already covered by the HyperShift skip check (line 105-106)
    - Detection: IsAroHCP() checks for MANAGED_SERVICE=ARO-HCP env var in control-plane-operator

  2. OSD (OpenShift Dedicated)
  - Runs on AWS or GCP with standard control plane architecture
  - Should NOT skip - uses regular TLS auto-collection like standard OCP
  - Note: Only ROSA (managed service on AWS) has the special behavior requiring a skip

  3. General Managed Service Detection
  - The codebase has IsManagedServiceCluster() (framework.go:2279) that checks for openshift-backplane namespace
  - This broadly detects OSD, ROSA, and other managed services but is not used for cert tests
  - This is intentional - not all managed services lack TLS auto-collection

  **Key Insight:**

  The distinction is based on control plane architecture, not managed service status:
  - Hosted/External Control Plane (HyperShift, ROSA, ARO HCP) → Skip
  - Self-hosted Control Plane (standard OCP, OSD, regular ARO) → Don't skip

----

## Changes

### Commit 1: Reapply PR #29074 (was reverted in #30358)
- Changes `testresult.Flakef()` to `g.Fail()` for certificate tests
- Removes TODO comments about making tests required
- Original PR: #29074
- This commit brings back the proper failure reporting mechanism

### Commit 2: Mark TLS certificate tests as informing
- Added import for `github.com/openshift-eng/openshift-tests-extension/pkg/ginkgo`
- Added `ote.Informing()` to both certificate tests:
  - "all tls artifacts must be registered"
  - "all registered tls artifacts must have no metadata violation regressions"

### Commit 3: Skip TLS certificate tests on ROSA clusters
- Added `IsRosaCluster()` function to `test/extended/util/framework.go`
- Skip certificate tests on ROSA clusters (similar to MicroShift and Hypershift)
- ROSA clusters do not auto-collect TLS certificates the same way as standard OpenShift clusters

## Behavior

After these changes:

**On standard OpenShift clusters:**
- Both certificate tests will continue to run in blocking CI jobs
- Tests use `g.Fail()` for proper failure reporting
- Tests have `ote.Informing()` label → **Non-blocking** (failures won't fail CI)
- Gather data about TLS artifacts and metadata violations without blocking PRs

**On ROSA, MicroShift, and Hypershift clusters:**
- Tests are skipped (these platforms don't auto-collect TLS the same way)

## Benefits
- Tests provide proper failure reports with `g.Fail()`
- Tests are marked as informing, so failures are recorded but don't block development
- We can gather data and stabilize the tests while work continues on certificate registration and metadata compliance
- Avoid running tests on platforms that don't support TLS auto-collection
- Once tests are stable, the `ote.Informing()` label can be removed to make them blocking again
