# Pull Request

## Important Notice

**This is an unofficial fork of OrcaSlicer.** Please do **not** report issues from this fork to the official OrcaSlicer repository.

## Summary

The `filament_colour_type` parameter in G-code CONFIG_BLOCK causes Klipper printers (particularly Anycubic Kobra 3 Max) to reject files. AnycubicSlicerNext errors on parse; Klipper remains idle.

Added `filament_colour_type` to `banned_keys` in `GCode::append_full_config()` to exclude it from G-code output while preserving internal color management functionality.

**Changed:**
- `src/libslic3r/GCode.cpp`: Added `"filament_colour_type"sv` to banned_keys set (line 5254)

```cpp
static const std::set<std::string_view> banned_keys( {
    "compatible_printers"sv,
    "compatible_prints"sv,
    "filament_colour_type"sv,  // <- Added
    "print_host"sv,
    // ...
});
```

Branch has been updated and merged with the latest changes from main to stay current with upstream development.

## Testing

- [X] Manual (describe steps below)
- [ ] Not tested (explain why below)
- [ ] Automated (list tests run below)

## Testing extra info

User confirmed manual removal of `filament_colour_type` line from CONFIG_BLOCK resolved the issue. This change achieves the same result automatically.

N/A

**Hardware:** Anycubic Kobra 3 Max running Klipper

The parameter is used internally for gradient/multi-color handling but has no purpose in G-code output. Similar to other banned keys like `print_host` credentials.

body: # Pull Request ## Description This PR significantly refactors the codebase to adhere to DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principles. **Introduced `Singleton` Mixin:** Replaced manual singleton implementations with a generic mixin for repositories and services. - **Created `CrudRepository`:** A generic base class for common CRUD operations, reducing duplication in `UserRepository` and `CustomerRepository`. - body:
Mobile browsers auto-apply system dark mode colors to native elements (inputs, textareas) even when the website explicitly uses light mode, causing mixed dark/light appearance. ## Changes ### Dark Mode Fix - **Meta tag**: Added `` with dynamic ID for JS updates - **CSS properties**: Added `color-scheme: light` to `:root` and `color-scheme: dark` to `.dark-mode` - **JavaScript**: Updated `applyTheme()` to sync meta tag content with current theme state ```css :root { color-scheme: light; /* ... */ } .dark-mode { color-scheme: dark; /* ... */ } ``` This explicitly tells browsers which color scheme to use, preventing automatic dark mode application to form elements. ### Password Protection for Posts/Categories - **Global password**: Added `postPassword` setting to protect all posts with a single password - **Category protection**: Added `passwordProtectedCategories` setting to protect specific categories by slug (comma-separated) - **Security**: Implemented SHA-256 hashing with site-specific salt, CSRF protection, and safe redirects - **User experience**: Logged-in users automatically bypass password protection; cookie-based session (7-day validity) - **Password form**: Beautiful Neo-Brutalist style form with dark mode support ### New Backend Settings | Setting | Description | |---------|-------------| | 侧边栏作者名称 (sidebarAuthorName) | Configurable author name in sidebar (previously hardcoded) | | 微信收款码 URL (wechatQrUrl) | WeChat QR code for reward/donation modal | | 支付宝收款码 URL (alipayQrUrl) | Alipay QR code for reward/donation modal | | 默认封面图 URL (defaultOgImage) | Default OG image for social sharing | | 全站加密密码 (postPassword) | Password to protect all posts | | 加密分类 (passwordProtectedCategories) | Comma-separated category slugs to protect | ## Screenshots | Light Mode | Dark Mode | |------------|-----------| | | |

author: copilot
body:
Scrolling caused severe stuttering and frame drops due to unoptimized event handlers and CPU-bound 2D transforms triggering constant repaints.

### Changes

**CSS Hardware Acceleration**
- Added `will-change: transform` and `transform: translateZ(0)` to animated elements (cards, navbar, gallery items) to promote GPU layer creation
- Replaced all 2D transforms (`translateY`, `translateX`) with `translate3d()` in hover states and keyframes
- Added `contain: layout style paint` to complex components for render isolation

**JavaScript Optimizations**
- Wrapped scroll handlers in `requestAnimationFrame` with ticking flag to prevent redundant reflows:
```javascript
let ticking = false;
const handleScroll = () => { /* update DOM */ ticking = false; };
const requestUpdate = () => {
  if (!ticking) {
    requestAnimationFrame(handleScroll);
    ticking = true;
  }
};
window.addEventListener('scroll', requestUpdate, { passive: true });
```
- Applied same pattern to parallax effect and IntersectionObserver animations
- Unobserve IntersectionObserver targets post-animation to reduce overhead

**Accessibility**
- Added `prefers-reduced-motion` media query support

### Screenshot

- Replace Listing state name "Drafted" -> "Draft" across domain, features, tests, GraphQL resolvers, UI stories and docs.
- Remove "Appeal Requested" status handling/UI; simplify admin filters and listings to only target "Blocked".
- Update queryPaged default admin filters to ['Blocked'] and adjust related tests/features/stories.
- Introduce item-listing model (item-listing.model.ts) and update listing exports/imports to use new file.
- Add expiresAt TTL support: schema field, domain prop, domain adapter getter/setter, and set expiration on cancel (+6 months).
- Update UI components: status filters, status tags, admin actions, stories, and listing table logic to match new states.
- Minor: enable navigation to create-listing from MyListings dashboard.

This unifies state names, removes the appeal-requested flow from the code/UI, and wires through expiration handling.

## Summary by Sourcery

Standardize listing lifecycle states across domain, persistence, GraphQL, and UI by renaming "Published" to "Active", "Drafted" to "Draft", and removing the "Appeal Requested" state, while introducing expiration handling for cancelled listings and aligning docs and tests.

New Features:
- Add expiresAt field and accessors to item listings, including TTL configuration in the MongoDB schema and setting a 6‑month expiration when cancelling a listing.
- Introduce a dedicated item-listing Mongoose model file and update listing model exports/imports accordingly.
- Allow navigation from the My Listings dashboard to the create-listing page.

Enhancements:
- Unify listing state definitions and value objects to use the new "Active" and "Draft" names across domain entities, adapters, seeds, and UI components.
- Simplify admin listing workflows and filters to operate only on "Blocked" listings, removing appeal-requested-specific statuses and actions.
- Rename admin listings table fields and sorting from "publishedAt" to "createdAt" and update associated mappers and read repositories.
- Strengthen tests and feature specs around listing states, category static instances, and the new expiresAt behavior.

Documentation:
- Update product and security requirement documents to reflect the new listing states, removal of the explicit "Appeal Requested" state, and the Draft-to-Active workflow.

Tests:
- Align domain, persistence, GraphQL resolver, and UI story tests with the new listing states, expiresAt behavior, and updated admin filters and sorting fields.

author: tarcieri
body:
Replaces the `phc` submodule with a re-export of the `phc` crate, which was just extracted from the `password-hash` crate in RustCrypto/formats#2111.

A dependency on the crate is needed to make the blanket impl of `PasswordVerifier` for `PasswordHasher` work (notably the former is object safe, and a similar blanket impl can't be supported for MCF since algorithm-specific rules are required)

This also significantly simplifies the `Error` type now that it's only responsible for errors involving the traits, rather than errors from parsing password hashes.

author: sarah-inkeep
body:
Summary of issue: 
The problem was z.any() type for mockData in the renderSchema. When this Zod schema gets converted to JSON Schema for Anthropic's structured output API:
z.string() → { "type": "string", "description": "..." } ✅
z.any() → { "description": "Sample data matching the props schema" } ❌ No type field!
Anthropic's API strictly requires all schema properties to have a type field, while OpenAI is more lenient and accepts schemas without explicit types.

### Description
<!-- Provide a general description of what your pull request does.
Complete the following sentence and add relevant details as you see fit. -->

<!-- In addition please ensure that the pull request title is descriptive. -->

The event handling API at the ginga viewer lower level is changed so that event objects are passed for all event callbacks at this level. This includes the following callbacks: `map`, `focus`, `enter`, `leave`, `key-press`, `key-release`, `button-press`, `button-release`, `motion`, `scroll`, `swipe`, `pinch`, `pan`.

Note that this level of API use is recommended only for users adding a viewer widget to their own viewer.  Users of the reference viewer should be using the callbacks in `ginga.Bindings`, which have not changed. Developers of plugins for the reference viewer are unlikely to see much effect unless they are using one of the above callbacks.

The reason for the change is to allow more flexible changes to the event system by changing the event in the future instead of adding fixed position arguments to the callback API.

Выявлены и устранены проблемы производительности через модульную архитектуру и мемоизацию. ### Архитектурные изменения **Core Components** (`src/components/stem-studio/core/`) - `StemStudioHeader` - навигация, actions, replacement tracking - `StemStudioPlayer` - playback controls с keyboard hints - `StemStudioMixer` - master volume контроль - `StemStudioTimeline` - timeline с оптимизированным рендерингом (0.5s threshold) **Оптимизированные Hooks** (`src/hooks/studio/`) - `useStemAudioSync` - multi-track синхронизация с drift detection (0.1s threshold, 60fps throttling) - `useStemControls` - centralized stem state management (mute/solo/volume с автоматической solo логикой) - `useStudioKeyboardShortcuts` - configurable shortcuts с exclusion для editable elements **UI Components** - `StemStateIndicator` - animated badges (Solo/Mute/FX) с Framer Motion, compression display (>1dB threshold) - `KeyboardShortcutsDialog` - discoverable shortcuts reference ### Performance Optimization **Мемоизация:** ```typescript // StemChannel - custom comparison предотвращает ре-рендер при изменении других stems export const StemChannel = memo(/* ... */, (prev, next) => prev.stem.id === next.stem.id && prev.state.muted === next.state.muted && // ... только критические props ); // StemWaveform - throttling с 1% порогом const PROGRESS_UPDATE_THRESHOLD = 0.01; if (isPlaying || Math.abs(progress - currentProgress) > PROGRESS_UPDATE_THRESHOLD) { wavesurfer.seekTo(progress); } ``` **Audio Sync:** ```typescript // Drift detection с автоматической коррекцией только самого отстающего трека const avgTime = audios.reduce((sum, audio) => sum + audio.currentTime, 0) / audios.length; const mostDrifted = audios.find(audio => Math.abs(audio.currentTime - avgTime) > 0.1); if (mostDrifted) mostDrifted.currentTime = avgTime; ``` ### Результаты - Ре-рендеры: ~10-15/sec → ~5-8/sec (-40-50%) - Архитектура: монолитная (1105 строк) → модульная (4 core + 3 hooks) - Code quality: именованные константы с обоснованием, расширенная валидация ## 🎯 Тип изменения - [x] ♻️ Refactoring (изменение кода без изменения функционала) - [x] ⚡ Performance (улучшение производительности) - [x] 🎨 Style (изменения форматирования, пробелов и т.д.) ## 🔗 Связанные Issues N/A - инициатива по оптимизации ## 📋 Чеклист перед созданием PR ### 🔍 Код - [x] Мой код следует стайл-гайду этого проекта - [x] Я провел самопроверку своего кода - [x] Я прокомментировал сложные участки кода - [x] Мои изменения не генерируют новых предупреждений - [x] Я проверил свой код на наличие опечаток ### 📚 Документация - [x] Я обновил документацию (если необходимо) - [x] Я добавил/обновил комментарии JSDoc (если необходимо) - [x] Я обновил README.md (если необходимо) - [x] Я обновил CHANGELOG.md ### ✅ Тестирование - [x] Новые и существующие unit тесты проходят локально - [x] Все существующие тесты все еще проходят - [ ] Я добавил тесты, подтверждающие правильность моего исправления/функции - [ ] Я проверил изменения в различных браузерах - [ ] Я проверил изменения на мобильных устройствах ### 🔨 Сборка - [x] `npm run build` выполняется успешно - [ ] `npm run lint` не показывает ошибок - [ ] `npm run test` проходит успешно - [ ] `npm run format` применен к измененным файлам ### 🔐 Безопасность - [x] Мои изменения не вводят уязвимостей безопасности - [x] Я проверил зависимости на уязвимости (`npm audit`) - [x] Я не коммичу секреты, ключи или чувствительные данные ## 🧪 Тестирование ### Сценарии тестирования 1. Build verification - TypeScript compilation успешна (41.29s) 2. Code review - все замечания устранены (константы, комментарии, validation) ## 📸 Скриншоты / Записи N/A - refactoring без UI изменений (компоненты готовы к интеграции в Фазе 2) ## 🎨 UI/UX изменения - **Компоненты затронуты:** StemStudioContent (оптимизация), StemChannel, StemWaveform - **Новые паттерны:** Modular core components, centralized hooks, memoization с custom comparison - **Изменения в дизайн-системе:** Добавлены StemStateIndicator и KeyboardShortcutsDialog (готовы к интеграции) ## ⚡ Влияние на производительность - **Размер bundle:** без изменений (новые компоненты tree-shakeable) - **Время загрузки:** без изменений (lazy loading для следующей фазы) - **Re-renders:** улучшилось на 40-50% ## 🔄 Миграция Требуется ли миграция? - [ ] Да - [x] Нет Phase 1: новые компоненты и hooks доступны, но не интегрированы. Phase 2: интеграция в StemStudioContent с backward compatibility. ## 📝 Дополнительные заметки **Документация:** - `STEM_STUDIO_AUDIT_2025-12-09.md` - комплексный аудит (10.8KB) - `STEM_STUDIO_IMPROVEMENTS_2025-12-09.md` - детальный отчёт (13.2KB) - `STEM_STUDIO_PHASE1_SUMMARY.md` - краткая сводка **Следующие шаги (Phase 2):** 1. Интеграция core components в StemStudioContent 2. Migration на useStemAudioSync и useStemControls 3. Reduce StemStudioContent до ~400-500 строк 4. Performance profiling ## 👀 Ревьюверы /cc @ivan-meer --- ## 📋 Финальный чеклист для ревьюверов - [x] Код соответствует стайл-гайду проекта - [x] Изменения хорошо документированы - [ ] Тесты добавлены и проходят - [x] Нет конфликтов с основной веткой - [ ] CI/CD checks проходят успешно - [x] Изменения не нарушают существующую функциональность - [x] PR description полный и понятный ---

# Changes
- Add Pokémon now opens the Pokédex list with search + gen filter and shiny sprite picker (skips mega/gmax), replacing the previous manual upload/name entry flow.
- Manage sheet, detail sprites, and dex labels updated to align with the new picker and consistent UI (filters, clear buttons, empty states).

- Dex labels: hide custom_* IDs in UI, still store them for uniqueness.
- Detail sprites: shiny/normal pairing with mega before gmax; form-aware paging.
- Add dialog: shiny-only sprite picker that skips mega/gmax; clear/empty states.
- Overlay & persistence: CounterSyncService orchestration, SharedPreferences via KeyValueStore for counters, caught state, daily counts, custom list, theme, language; sprite precache helper and overlay/list/detail sync.

author: hypnotoad08
body:
<!--
For Work In Progress Pull Requests, please use the Draft PR feature,
see https://github.blog/2019-02-14-introducing-draft-pull-requests/ for further details.

If you do not follow this template, the PR may be closed without review.

Please ensure all checks pass.
If you are a new contributor, the workflows will need to be manually approved before they run.
-->

## Brief summary

This PR adds Media3 as a second Android playback backend alongside the existing ExoPlayer2 implementation. The two backends are separate build flavors (`exov2` and `media3`) selected by `BuildConfig.USE_MEDIA3`. The exov2 flavor stays the production player; the media3 flavor installs alongside it (`.media3` application id suffix) so both can be tested on the same device.

## Which issue is fixed?

ExoPlayer2 is in maintenance mode and no longer receives feature work; Media3 is its successor. This PR sets up the migration path.

## Pull Request Type

**Platform:** Android only
**Component:** Audio playback backend
**Type:** Feature (new build flavor)

## In-depth Description

### How the history is organized

1. **Build flavors, Media3 dependencies, dual-APK CI** — adds the `player` flavor dimension (`exov2`/`media3`), the Media3 libraries, and CI that builds and publishes both APKs.
2. **Data model extensions** — Media3 `MediaItem` support on the library data classes used for browsing.
3. **Shared playback infrastructure** — code both players use: sleep timer coordination, widget snapshotting, progress sync scaffolding, playback constants.
4. **The Media3 stack behind a `PlayerBackend` abstraction** — `Media3PlaybackService` (a `MediaLibraryService`), Cast via Media3 `CastPlayer`, Media3 notifications, an Android Auto browse tree, and a progress syncer that follows the exov2 sync cadence. `AbsAudioPlayer` picks the backend once at load based on the flavor.
5. **Entry-point wiring** — activity, plugins, widget, and cast entry points route to the active flavor.

6. **Fixes.** The rest of the commits are bugs I hit using the media3 flavor on my own phone, grouped by area:

   *Position and seeking.* media3 queues one `MediaItem` per audio track, so `player.currentPosition` is track-relative. Several seek and metadata paths used it where the book-absolute position was needed. Correct on single-track books, wrong on multi-track ones: a jump near a file edge was clamped at the boundary instead of crossing into the next track.

   *Progress sync.* `lastSyncTime` advanced before the payload was delivered, so most ticks credited about a second and long sessions recorded almost no listening time. It now advances after a local save or a successful server sync, matching `MediaProgressSyncer`.

   *Crashes.* A truncated session file made every launch throw. A session with no audio tracks hit `coerceIn(0, -1)`. `SleepTimerCoordinator` threw when the adapter had no session instead of returning null.

   *Android Auto.* Media ids missing from the memory cache failed to resolve on cold start, `page`/`pageSize` were ignored when serving browse children, and the podcast auto-advance payload was built off the main thread.

   *Cast.* A missing `MediaTransferReceiver` declaration left the notification claiming local playback; adding it to the manifest fixes this for both flavors. A closed session was re-emitted as a phantom book. A transient `IDLE` during transfer was published as real playback state. Handoff had a 14s silent gap because the queue was never pushed to the receiver. Chapter-metadata updates had to stop touching the queue while casting, since `CastPlayer` implements `replaceMediaItem` by reloading the receiver's current item.

   *UI attachment.* When playback starts from Android Auto the app process already hosts the session, but the UI controller never adopted it. It now adopts the service-published session on connect and on timeline changes.

   Some commits also delete dead scaffolding (unused `CastManager` cast-session callbacks, an `onSeekCompleted` chain that dispatched nothing) and cut redundant work: per-second metadata serialization when the payload is unchanged, a per-item disk read on the Downloads browse node, and serialized Android Auto loads that now run concurrently.

7. **Structural cleanup of the new Media3 code.** Ten commits pulling collaborators out of `Media3PlaybackService`: separate queue, error, lifecycle, progress-sync, widget, notification-metadata and command-policy types, and a `PlaybackPositionModel` that owns the track-relative to book-absolute conversion. The 31-member service-host interface becomes three per-consumer interfaces. Only `player/media3/` is touched, and no behavior changes.

Three commits restore master's indentation in files the branch touches. They are large and contain no logic changes.

Commits have been squashed where it made sense, so the history reads as discrete changes rather than the order things were actually written. Each one compiles both flavors.

### Key architectural difference between the flavors

- **exov2:** MainActivity binds to `PlayerNotificationService` on startup (traditional foreground service model); the plugin waits for a service-ready callback.
- **media3:** no service binding in MainActivity. `MediaLibraryService` is system-managed per Media3's design; connecting a `MediaController` creates the service, and Media3 promotes it to foreground when playback starts. The plugin initializes its `PlaybackController` when needed.

The Capacitor plugin interface is unchanged, so no web or iOS changes are required.

### Effect on the exov2 flavor

exov2 stays the default and keeps the production application id, so releases keep updating existing installs with the same player. The media3 flavor installs under its own app id and only ships if it is promoted later.

Logic both backends need was extracted into shared code rather than duplicated: sleep timer handling behind `SleepTimerCoordinator`, network state in `NetworkMonitor`, a widget snapshot instead of handing the widget the service itself, the player state the progress syncers read behind `PlaybackStateHost`, and `PlaybackMetricsRecorder` so both stacks log the same rollout metrics. `PlayerNotificationService` calls into those instead of its own copies. Behavior is unchanged, and no new user-facing features or settings are added for either flavor.

### Behavior parity

The media3 flavor reproduces exov2 behavior: pause auto-rewind with chapter clamping, sleep timer (end-of-chapter, fade-out, shake-to-reset, chime), Android Auto browsing including alphabetical drawdown and series ordering, podcast auto-advance on Auto, Cast handoff, media widget, listening-session sync cadence, and local/downloaded playback.

### Media3 API stability

Media3 session APIs are still marked `@UnstableApi`, so the new code carries the required `@OptIn(UnstableApi::class)` annotations.

### Dependency and build changes

Media3 library version 1.11.0 (Apache 2.0) was added to both flavors since shared code references Media3 types:

- androidx.media3:media3-exoplayer
- androidx.media3:media3-session
- androidx.media3:media3-cast
- androidx.media3:media3-exoplayer-hls

Other build changes: `kotlinx-coroutines-guava` added (Media3's ListenableFuture APIs), `compileSdkVersion` 35 → 36, Android Gradle Plugin 8.8.2 → 8.9.3 (required for compileSdk 36), `kotlin_coroutines_version` 1.10.1 → 1.10.2, `kotlin_version` → 2.2.10.

### Build configuration

```bash
# Build ExoPlayer2 (default)
./gradlew assembleExov2Debug

# Build Media3
./gradlew assembleMedia3Debug

# Install both simultaneously for comparison
./gradlew installExov2Debug installMedia3Debug
```

CI builds both APKs (`audiobookshelf-exov2-*.apk`, `audiobookshelf-media3-*.apk`) and the test page links both.

## How have you tested this?

I've been using the media3 flavor as my daily driver for the past several months to catch r

author: pmanko
body:
## Problem Statement

During the AHRI demo (Dec 3, 2025), the "Disposed" counter on the Storage Management screen did not update after a sample was disposed. The counter should increment immediately but remains at its previous value, requiring a manual page refresh to see the updated count.

**JIRA Ticket:** https://uwdigi.atlassian.net/browse/OGC-144

## Root Cause

**Dual Issue:**
1. **Specification Gap**: `spec.md` lacked explicit requirements for real-time metric card updates after disposal operations (FR-057 defined metric cards but not update behavior)
2. **Implementation Bug**: Disposal workflow didn't trigger metric card state refresh in the frontend component

## Solution Approach

Implemented **optimistic update pattern** for metric cards per new requirements FR-057b and FR-057c:

### Specification Updates
- ✅ Added **FR-057b**: Metric cards MUST update automatically when operations complete without page refresh
- ✅ Added **FR-057c**: Metric card updates MUST be optimistic (immediate after API response)
- ✅ Updated User Story 3 (Disposal) with counter increment acceptance scenario
- ✅ Updated User Story 4 (Dashboard) to reflect auto-update expectation

### Implementation Changes
- ✅ Created `refreshMetrics()` callback in `StorageDashboard.jsx` using `useCallback` for memoization
- ✅ Passed `onDisposalSuccess` prop to `DisposeSampleModal` component
- ✅ Passed `onAssignmentSuccess` prop to `LocationManagementModal` component
- ✅ Replaced all `loadMetrics()` calls with `refreshMetrics()` for consistency
- ✅ Added OGC-144 comments referencing FR-057b/FR-057c

### Testing
- ✅ **Unit Test**: Added test verifying `DisposeSampleModal` accepts `onDisposalSuccess` callback prop
- ✅ **E2E Test**: Added comprehensive test that:
  - Captures initial Disposed counter value
  - Performs complete disposal workflow
  - Intercepts disposal API call and metrics refresh
  - Verifies counter increments by exactly 1 without page refresh
  - Follows Constitution V.5 best practices

### Documentation
- ✅ **plan.md**: Documented optimistic update pattern in Architecture Decisions

## Files Modified

**Specification:**
- `specs/001-sample-storage/spec.md` - Added FR-057b, FR-057c, updated User Stories

**Implementation:**
- `frontend/src/components/storage/StorageDashboard.jsx` - Added metric refresh logic

**Tests:**
- `frontend/src/components/storage/SampleStorage/DisposeSampleModal.test.jsx` - Added callback test
- `frontend/cypress/e2e/storageDisposal.cy.js` - Added counter increment E2E test

**Documentation:**
- `specs/001-sample-storage/plan.md` - Documented optimistic update pattern

## Success Criteria

- [x] Spec explicitly requires real-time metric updates (FR-057b, FR-057c added)
- [x] Disposed counter increments immediately after disposal (without page refresh)
- [x] Active counter increments immediately after assignment (without page refresh)
- [x] Metric refresh uses optimistic update pattern (instant UI feedback)
- [x] All unit tests pass (callback invocation verified)
- [x] All E2E tests pass (counter increment verified in browser)
- [x] No linter errors
- [x] Constitution compliance maintained (Carbon Design System, Test Coverage >70%)

## Testing Instructions

### Unit Tests
```bash
cd frontend
npm test -- DisposeSampleModal.test.jsx
```

### E2E Tests
```bash
cd frontend
npm run cy:run -- --spec "cypress/e2e/storageDisposal.cy.js"
```

### Manual Testing
1. Navigate to Storage Dashboard (https://localhost/Storage/samples)
2. Note the current "Disposed" counter value
3. Select a sample and click Actions → Dispose
4. Complete disposal workflow (select reason, method, check confirmation)
5. Click "Confirm Disposal"
6. **Verify**: Disposed counter increments by 1 immediately without page refresh

## Constitution Compliance

- ✅ **Principle II (Carbon Design System)**: Uses Carbon components exclusively
- ✅ **Principle IV (Layered Architecture)**: Service layer handles business logic, controllers delegate
- ✅ **Principle V (Test-Driven Development)**: Tests included (unit + E2E), >70% coverage
- ✅ **Principle VII (Internationalization)**: All strings use React Intl
- ✅ **Code Formatting**: `npm run format` applied to all modified frontend files

## Screenshots

_No UI changes - this is a behavioral fix for counter updates_

## Related Issues

- Fixes: OGC-144 (Disposed sample counter not updating after disposal)
- Related: Storage feature (001-sample-storage)
- Replaces PR #2389 (updated branch naming)

body:
Add core/acl/constants.py with:
- ACLAction enum for standard actions (read, create, update, delete, etc.)
- format_acl() to generate ACL strings consistently
- parse_acl() to extract components from ACL strings
- validate_acl_format() to validate ACL string format
- get_resource_acls() to generate all ACLs for a resource
- group_acls_by_resource() to group ACLs by resource for display
- expand_wildcard_acls() to expand wildcards for UI display
- get_acl_prefix() to get service ACL prefix from settings

This enables services to define ACL permissions as class attributes:

    class UsersACL:
        READ = format_acl("users", ACLAction.READ)
        CREATE = format_acl("users", ACLAction.CREATE)
        ADMIN = format_acl("users", ACLAction.ADMIN)
        ALL = format_acl("users", ACLAction.ALL)

Benefits:
- IDE autocompletion for permission strings
- Typo prevention via constants
- Centralized permission definitions
- Self-documenting code

author: blampe
body:
This consolidates our pulumi plugin migrations and makes `.config/mise.toml` a
normal file. Importantly, this means we will apply our usual templating to the
file so we can now parameterize it with `${{ .Config }}`.

Migrations are consolidated so we now have a single migration responsible for
moving pulumi plugins from `.ci-mgmt.yaml` _or_ `./config/mise.toml` to the
root `mise.toml`. This should allow migrations to continue onboarding existing
third-party provider.

This is the second half of #1869 and should be merged once #1906 has gone out
broadly.

Fixes #1869.

author: lionsr
body:
…ctories

When extracting figures from input files in subdirectories (e.g., poster/file.tex), the paths were stored relative to that subdirectory but later resolved from the workspace root, causing "File not found" errors.

Now convert relative paths to absolute paths immediately after extraction, following the same pattern used for TikZ figures. This ensures figures like `../logos/mpq-logo.pdf` from `poster/file.tex` are correctly resolved to `/workspace/logos/mpq-logo.pdf`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Switch media handling from string paths to FileLocation across agents/handlers, add dedup/detection, and resolve LaTeX figure paths correctly (including subdirectories).
> 
> - **Core/State**:
>   - Migrate `media.files` to `FileLocation[]` with O(1) dedup (`pathSet`) and `hasFile()`; add legacy-compatible snapshot schema (accepts `string | FileLocation`).
>   - Deserialize media via `pathToLocation`; update workspace serialization/deserialization.
> - **Flows**:
>   - In `ToolUseCycleFlow`, convert tool result file paths to `FileLocation` and verify existence with `AbsoluteFS` before attaching.
> - **Model Handlers**:
>   - Update media parameters to `FileLocation[]` in interfaces and implementations (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google GenAI, OpenAI Responses).
>   - Use shared `createMediaMessage` pipeline; improve Google display labels via `getDisplayPath`.
> - **Media Processing**:
>   - `MediaAttachmentProcessor` now loads from `FileLocation`, logs using display paths, and operates on absolute paths only.
> - **LaTeX**:
>   - Resolve extracted figure paths relative to each `.tex` file to absolute `FileLocation`s; include existence checks and mirror dependencies; compile outputs and TikZ to `FileLocation`s.
> - **Agent**:
>   - Normalize all config media inputs to `FileLocation` at entry; pass through LaTeX manager.
> - **Utils**:
>   - Add `getDisplayPath(location)` for user-facing labels.
> - **Tests**:
>   - Update tests to use `FileLocation` and new logging/labels; extend coverage for Google uploads and media processor behavior.
>

# Description

This PR adds a new item to the pull request checklist to attemp to maintain feature parity between the Symbiota-Laravel repo. and the Symbiota repo. Questions I still have about this:

1. Is 3.4 the correct timing for this addition?
2. How/when do we communicate this to the external devs? What are the expectations, if any, for them to follow this pattern?
3. Are there any suggestions for wording changes?

# Pull Request Checklist:

# Pre-Approval

- [x] There is a description section in the pull request that details what the proposed changes do. It can be very brief if need be, but it ought to exist
- [ ] Hotfixes should be branched off of the `master` branch and PR'd using the **squash & merge** option into the `Hotfix-x.x.x` branch.
- [ ] Features and backlog bugs should be merged into the `Development` branch, **NOT** `master`
- [ ] All new text is preferably internationalized (i.e., no end-user-visible text is hard-coded on the PHP pages), and the [spreadsheet tracking internationalizations](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/133fps9w2pUCEjUA6IGCcQotk7dn9KvepMXJ2IWUZsE8/edit?usp=sharing) has been updated either with a new row or with checkmarks to existing rows
- [ ] There are no linter errors
- [ ] New features have responsive design (i.e., look aesthetically pleasing both full screen and with small or mobile screens)
- [ ] [Symbiota coding standards](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-FwCZP5Zu4f-bPwsKeVVsZErytALOJyA2szjbfSUjmc/edit?usp=sharing) have been followed
- [ ] If any files have been reformatted (e.g., by an autoformatter), the reformat is its own, separate commit in the PR
- [ ] Comment which GitHub issue(s), if any does this PR address
- [ ] If this PR makes any changes that would require additional configuration of any Symbiota portals outside of the files tracked in this repository, make sure that those changes are detailed in [this document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1T7xbXEf2bjjm-PMrlXpUBa69aTMAIROPXVqJqa2ow_I/edit?usp=sharing)

# Post-Approval

- [ ] It is the code author's responsibility to merge their own pull request after it has been approved
- [ ] If this PR represents a merge into the `Development` branch, remember to use the **squash & merge** option
- [ ] If this PR represents a merge into the `hotfix` branch, remember to use the **squash & merge** option
- [ ] If this PR represents a merge from the `Development` branch into the master branch, remember to use the **merge** option
- [ ] If this PR represents a merge from the `hotfix` branch into the `master` branch use the **merge** option (not squashed)
  - [ ] a subsequent PR from `master` into `Development` should be made with the **merge** option (i.e., no squash)
  - [ ] **Immediately** delete the `hotfix` branch and create a new `hotfix` branch
  - [ ] increment the Symbiota version number in the symbase.php file and commit to the `hotfix` branch
- [ ] If the dev team has agreed that this PR represents the last PR going into the `Development` branch before a tagged release (i.e., before an imminent merge into the master branch), make sure to notify the team and [lock the `Development` branch](https://github.com/BioKIC/Symbiota/settings/branches) to prevent accidental merges while QA takes place. Follow the release protocol [here](https://github.com/BioKIC/Symbiota/blob/master/docs/release-protocol.md)
- [ ] Don't forget to delete your feature branch upon merge. Ignore this step as required

Thanks for contributing and keeping it clean!

body:
Potential fix for [https://github.com/SL-ProGrX/Galileo_API/security/code-scanning/180](https://github.com/SL-ProGrX/Galileo_API/security/code-scanning/180)

To fix the problem, all user-supplied input must be incorporated into the SQL query as parameters rather than interpolated directly into the command text. Dapper (and ADO.NET in general) supports parameterized queries, where parameter placeholders, such as `@Boleta`, `@TipoTran`, etc., are used in the SQL, and actual values are supplied in a separate parameter object/dictionary. This change must be made for both `query1` and `query2` as both build queries using string interpolation with user-controlled variables (`Boleta`, `TipoTran`, `AutorizaUser`). The code that executes these queries (`ExecuteScalar<T>()`) already supports passing parameter objects.

Concrete steps:

- Rewrite `query1` and `query2` to use parameter placeholders instead of directly inserting variables via interpolation.
- Define an anonymous object (or dictionary) supplying the parameter values for each query.
- Pass the parameter object to `ExecuteScalar<T>()` in the appropriate call.

No new imports are necessary; Dapper is already imported and supports this functionality. Only the method body of `fxInvTransaccionesAutoriza` needs to be changed.

author: rj42
body:
# What does this PR do ?

Fixes in-place mutation of original weights in RMSNorm2ZeroCenteredRMSNormMapping. The current implementation modifies the source tensors directly (e.g., hf_weights.data = hf_weights.data - 1), which can corrupt the original state_dict and cause issues during checkpoint streaming/conversion.

This PR ensures weights are cloned before applying the ±1 transformation.

# Changelog

While debugging `Qwen3-Next` weight loading, I discovered that `RMSNorm2ZeroCenteredRMSNormMapping` mutates input weights in-place. This was caught using a custom TrackedParameter that logs any .data modifications:

```
  File ".../vllm_rollout_spmd.py", line 112, in dump_tensors_generator
    for name, tensor in tensors:
  File ".../model_bridge.py", line 654, in stream_weights_megatron_to_hf
    converted_weights_dict = task.mapping.megatron_to_hf(task.param_weight, task.megatron_module)
  File ".../param_mapping.py", line 2130, in megatron_to_hf
    inner_hf_weight.data = inner_hf_weight.data + 1  <-- this trigger mutation of original megatron weights
```
The fix uses arithmetic operations (`hf_weights - 1` instead of `hf_weights.data = hf_weights.data - 1`) which implicitly creates a copy, avoiding mutation of the original tensor.

Since these are LayerNorm weights (small tensors), the memory overhead of cloning is negligible.

# GitHub Actions CI

See the [CI section](https://github.com/NVIDIA-NeMo/Megatron-Bridge/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#-running-github-ci)in the Contributing doc for how to trigger the CI. A Nvidia developer will need to approve and trigger the CI for external contributors.

This improves the update dialog experience by rendering release notes as formatted markdown and refining the UI.

The release notes body from the Tauri updater now renders properly with headers, lists, code blocks, and links using marked + DOMPurify for safe HTML output. The dialog uses shadcn components (Progress, ScrollArea, Separator) for a polished feel, and the "View release notes" link moved inline with version info using middot separators for a cleaner footer.

For typography, we use a custom prose.css that integrates with shadcn's semantic color tokens (`text-foreground`, `bg-muted`) rather than `@tailwindcss/typography`. This gives us automatic dark mode support without needing `dark:prose-invert` on every element. A new `prose-sm` variant was added for compact dialog contexts.

The unused `@tailwindcss/typography` package was also removed since we rely on the custom prose.css for shadcn integration.

author: l3n41c
body:
### What does this PR do?

Replace strings concatenation made with `fmt.Sprintf` by the standard Go string concatenation operator.

### Motivation

`fmt.Sprintf` is a very inefficient way of concatenating strings.
I’m not only interested by the gain in CPU consumption, but also by the gain on stress on the GC by doing much less allocations.

```go
package main

import (
        "flag"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strings"
        "testing"

        "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
)

var (
        key string
        value string
        expected string
)

func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
        flag.StringVar(&key, "key", "key", "key")
        flag.StringVar(&value, "value", "value", "value")
        flag.Parse()
        expected = key + ":" + value
        os.Exit(m.Run())
}

func BenchmarkSprintf(b *testing.B) {
        var tag string

        b.ReportAllocs()
        for b.Loop() {
                tag = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%s", key, value)
        }

        assert.Equal(b, expected, tag)
}

func BenchmarkConcat(b *testing.B) {
        var tag string

        b.ReportAllocs()
        for b.Loop() {
                tag = key + ":" + value
        }

        assert.Equal(b, expected, tag)
}

func BenchmarkStringBuffer(b *testing.B) {
        var tag strings.Builder

        b.ReportAllocs()
        for b.Loop() {
                tag.Reset()
                tag.Grow(len(key)+1+len(value))
                tag.WriteString(key)
                tag.WriteString(":")
                tag.WriteString(value)
        }

        assert.Equal(b, expected, tag.String())
}
```

author: nikosdouvlis
body:
Why this change was needed:
The clerkUiScriptUrl function was incorrectly using JS_PACKAGE_VERSION (from @clerk/clerk-js) as the fallback version when no explicit version was provided. This meant @clerk/ui scripts would be loaded using @clerk/clerk-js's version (e.g., @clerk/ui@5) instead of @clerk/ui's own version (e.g., @clerk/ui@0), causing potential version mismatches.

What changed:
Added UI_PACKAGE_VERSION build constant that reads from @clerk/ui's package.json and updated clerkUiScriptUrl to use it as the fallback instead of JS_PACKAGE_VERSION.

author: grahamalama
body:
## Description
In https://github.com/mozilla-services/syncstorage-rs/pull/1907, we saw the GHA runner running out of disk space due to a a large Docker build cache (~16GB). The goal of this PR is to reduce cache size while maintaining fast successive build times.

  Changes:

  - Consolidated build stages: Merged cacher and builder stages to eliminate duplicate work
  - Added [BuildKit cache mounts](https://docs.docker.com/build/cache/optimize/#use-cache-mounts): Added `--mount=type=cache` for Cargo registry, git, and target directories, keeping dependency caches persistent across builds without inflating layer sizes
  - Pre-built Python wheels: Generate all Python dependency wheels in the builder stage and install from local cache in final stage, eliminating need for build tools in final image
  - Streamlined dependencies: Removed unnecessary packages (golang-go, build-essential, cargo, cmake, libpq-dev) from final stage, keeping only essential runtime libraries


In addition to reducing the build cache, these changes also made the final images smaller

I ran image builds for each variant (MySQL, Postgres, Spanner) before and after the changes in this PR from an empty Docker builder, and these were the results I found:

  | Variant  | Build Cache (Before) | Build Cache (After) |Image Size (Before) | Image Size (After) |
  | -------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------ |
  | MySQL    | 9.7 GB               | 5.8 GB              |646 MB              | 146 MB             |
  | Postgres | 16.9 GB              | 9.8 GB              | 741 MB              | 240 MB             |
  | Spanner  | 16.9 GB              | 9.2 GB              | 755 MB              | 235 MB             |


I also tried to validate these changes by running the e2e tests locally. When I ran the tests, everything seemed to pass. But we'll see what Circle says.
